## Owner decision — unpinned installation under an independence bound is allowed, 2026-11-04

Scope: the question that comment 78000001 queued after withdrawing B: whether a new unpinned installation is allowed on a machine under a declared independence bound. The owner selected "Allow, as on 11-02". The panel had voted on cutting B, not on a refusal. Three of its readings favored forbidding the combination, as all three readings had on 11-02. The other two held that the current text already allows it, partly because a set spread across vendors may need a distribution the bundle does not pin.

The decision: under a declared independence bound, a new unpinned installation is allowed with the ordinary up-front acceptance, under `ARC-25`'s "the operator chooses it up front, from what the bundle lacks" and `SEC-14`'s "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it". The bound alone adds no prohibition and no further acceptance. There is no later acceptance window (comment 78000001), and a failed pinned check still never falls back: "A machine that began under a pin and failed it MUST NOT continue unpinned, whoever asks."

Known risk, accepted by the owner: an unpinned artifact source can substitute bootstrap content and an unchecked package-signer set across several members together, despite distinct configured models, singleton sessions and compliant footprint counts. Separate ordinary acceptances do not constrain that shared source. Pinned paths still share publisher and package-signer dependencies, so this is an additional unchecked path, not a claim that pinning proves independence.

For the later text work: the decision closes the item "An unpinned installation under an independence bound" in `TASKS.md` T47, and the ADR-0035 sentence "whether an unpinned installation is admissible under a declared independence bound, which nothing here settles", with a dated amendment there that states the decision and the accepted risk. It adds no new mechanism: no rule edit, no warning ceremony, no extra accepting act, no build gate, no profile permission slot and no conformance case. If the text work finds a normative rule that refuses this combination, it stops and reports rather than editing that rule.

Not selected: a refusal of new unpinned installations under a bound, a per-profile permit or forbid policy, refusal unless a tenant opts in, and a bundle-build rejection.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Robot rescue rekey moves the installation id but leaves the root's label stale; its ordinal may be unknown
description:
## The gap

`STA-17` says "If the old seed or an index is missing, direct re-entry and pass revocation
cannot finish. Robot machines can still be rekeyed through vendor-authenticated rescue
(`STA-15`)". `STA-22b` says "With no sheet, or for machines missing from a stale sheet, Robot
recovery installs keys from a fresh seed through vendor-authenticated rescue and re-reads host
pins; it does not guess old indices".

On that path the machine takes an index under the fresh seed, so the shown installation id's
machine component moves (`STG-20`). Replace's relabel job covers a dedicated machine reached by
direct re-entry. It does not cover this path. A root rekeyed this way keeps a label that no
longer equals the shown id. The install brief recognises only a label equal to the shown id as
its own installation, so the next return to rescue on that machine reads the machine's own root
as a predecessor and can steer toward erasing it.

## What is open

- **The ordinal.** The label is `<machine>-<n>`. With no sheet, or a stale one, the journal may
  hold no installation for the machine: `CHN-R7` says a non-destructive recovery "does not open
  an installation", and the credential format says Replace's migration "does not restart at
  zero". Nothing defines `n` here. Either a rule supplies it (for example from a readable,
  well-formed old root label), or nothing is written and the machine stays unmigrated until it
  is known.
- **The order.** No connection authenticated by the old key exists on this path, but the rescue
  ceremony ends in the installed system, so a connection authenticated by the new key can still
  be confirmed before a relabel. Whether the relabel then runs in the installed system or from
  rescue, and when the machine counts as migrated, is open.
- **The job.** `ARC-43`'s job list has no rescue rekey job yet.

## When it must be settled

Dedicated path only (cloud machines are destroyed and recreated). It must be settled before a
dedicated-server path is offered to an operator, which no stage before the third does; it sits
beside `CNF-84`'s Robot rescue case in `07-conformance.md`'s dedicated row.
close_reason: Landed: the dedicated rescue rekey keeps a proposed installation ordinal, relabels after the new-key login and removes only an identified old key; a machine left with an unidentified key fails CNF-5 until a read shows it clean (STA-17, STA-16, STG-20, ARC-43, credential format v6, install brief, CNF-117, ADR-0056, ADR-0045 note). Open points filed as tw-4mz.

comments.text:
## Owner decision — rescue ordinal accepted as a proposal, 2026-11-02

Selected B: during authorized rescue recovery of the same physical maintained machine, with no admissible saved history and a unique disk label such as `a-7`, the operator may explicitly accept 7 as a proposed current installation ordinal after checks against surviving facts. Migration to the new machine index b then uses `b-7`. A disk label is never adopted automatically.

The accepted number is a proposal, never historical proof. Earlier installation history remains explicitly unknown. Every retained identity, ordinal, installation observation and pin fact must be preserved; acceptance cannot override a contradiction or convert a missing comparison into a passed comparison. Known history still carries forward. Reading or accepting a label does not itself open a destructive installation, establish prior pin provenance, authenticate root contents, identify an old client key, revoke access or complete Replace.

This is an amendment requiring a new authority record and a versioned partial-history representation. Keep old-version validation unchanged: do not fabricate earlier groups, observations, pins or empty-history placeholders to encode the proposed ordinal. The credential format states: "Missing or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history." The new representation must round-trip the proposal's basis and the missing past without silently converting either into ordinary recovered history. It does not authorize future operations whose required facts or comparisons remain unavailable.

Follow-up A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02: the durable ordinal acceptance survives a worker restart when the operator resumes the unchanged recorded migration, for the same machine, root and destination allocation. Restart alone does not require accepting the ordinal again. Existing operational checks and retry restrictions still apply. This does not revive a worker's runtime authority, authorize a different target or changed proposal, permit an automatic retry, or establish that any possibly sent write completed. Sheet-import authority and changed-state conflicts are not selected by this restart decision.

Keep the captured observation, the target-bound operator act, genuine retained facts and relabel confirmation distinct. A failed acceptance append supplies no acceptance. The compact export must carry its own interpretable basis and unknown-history meaning, preserving all genuine facts and old-version validation. A pointer to missing journal evidence is insufficient. The retained acceptance basis and export meaning below carry these clarifications.

Job-order A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02, is an amendment: write the root label and read it back only after the installed system accepts a login authenticated with the new client key. The bounded harness job runs in the installed system. In the stated first-write case, a failed new-key login leaves the original `a-7` untouched. Reading a pinned host answer or authenticating to rescue is not installed-system acceptance of the client key. Keep the relabel's captured readback distinct from installed access, old-key revocation and whole Replace completion.

All three independent readings recommended this order. The alternative of writing in rescue but confirming from the installed system after login was offered separately and was not selected. Safe relabelling and readback of the supported mounted root still need implementation evidence. Prior source/rehearsal descriptions do not establish that capability. If the selected placement cannot be implemented safely, report the obstacle rather than silently falling back to rescue or adding another reboot cycle.

Display timing is technically settled as a presentation clarification within the selected model-free recovery: show `b-7` as the proposed or pending destination after acceptance, and distinguish allocation `b`, observed disk text `a-7`, installed access and label confirmation. Confirmed label/current-ID status needs the captured installed-system readback following the selected new-key login. Once a write has been sent, the earlier observed `a-7` is only an as-of observation, not an assertion about the disk's current label. Computing an internal destination immediately supplies no additional authority. This introduces no new session-binding or dispatch condition. Label confirmation, terminal job evidence, hold release and revocation remain separate facts.

Changed-label A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02, is an amendment: if an admissible captured observation of the same recorded root reports a changed label, such as `a-9` after acceptance of proposed `7` from `a-7`, before the relabel write, stop this bounded migration unfinished and preserve the discrepancy. Issue no relabel intent or label write in response to that conflict. Retain the acceptance, both observations, allocation and all existing history/pin associations under `7`; adopt no `9` and invent no installation boundary. The earlier new-key installation is not silently undone. This refusal creates no command hold without a sent command, grants no erasure, and implies no cleanup or revocation success. It adds no mandatory pre-write probe.

Two independent readings recommended stopping; the other recommended keeping `7` and writing `b-7`, and also offered a separate new confirmation of the same `7`. The owner selected stopping. Neither continuation nor that extra-confirmation alternative is selected. Existing unchanged-restart acceptance and no-auto-retry rules remain; preserving the captured discrepancy through restart must not silently normalize it into success.

Old-key A, selected by the owner on 2026-11-02, is an amendment: authorize the model-free rescue recovery flow to remove only the exact old client public key x independently identified by checked retained machine records for the same authorized machine. Removal follows successful installed-system login with the new key and the confirmed `b-7` readback. Preserve the new key and unrelated authorizations. Missing old private material is distinct from missing admissible old public identity; no impossible old-private-key login test is reported passed.

Unknown keys stay untouched and revocation is reported incomplete. Unknown public identity supplies no deletion target, no whole-file replacement and no new command hold. A removal from one named authorization source supports only that scoped effect, never whole-machine cleanup, termination of already accepted sessions, removal of persistence or application-secret rotation. Actual command/resource/destructive holds, durable intent, captured evidence and no-auto-retry rules remain. The stopped changed-label branch does not proceed to old-key removal.

All three independent readings selected exact identified-key removal; two explicitly classified rescue-path authorization as an amendment. Alternatives of replacing the whole key file, operator-selected deletion of an otherwise unidentified key, and admitting a seedless sheet for identification remain separately queued and unchosen.

Later old-sheet conflicts and any actual ordinary-session handoff during partial sheetless recovery remain queued. Installation acceptance and history decisions are recorded separately on tw-l1l; distinct T47 edges remain queued. Exact partial-history comparison/admission cases and formal coverage must be resolved without assuming lost history is empty or weakening a property. This record does not select those remaining policies. Keep the bead needing triage until the actual frontier is resolved and a bounded brief is ready.

Preserve the other settled boundaries: no universal installation-target approval or new reset gate; sheetless recovery grants no new destructive authority; current holds, pin checks, journal-before-send, no automatic retry, capability admission and completion truth remain. No theorem, requirement, assumption boundary, import refusal or control may be weakened to accommodate the amendment. Relevant normative owners are STA-17, STG-20, STA-16 and the credential format; the decision rationale belongs with ADR-0045. A later implementation changes the single normative owners together, then records the amendment.

The accepted observation and root provenance, target-bound operator act, genuine retained facts, relabel intent/result and captured confirmation remain separate linked facts. The compact versioned export carries an interpretable acceptance basis itself; a pointer to unavailable journal evidence is insufficient. No label component establishes an old seed-derived identity. A proposed base ordinal of 7 does not increment during non-destructive recovery; a later separately approved and otherwise admissible destructive reinstall derives 8 at its existing dispatch boundary while retaining the unknown past. This arithmetic waives no admission, pin, hold, retry, completion, capability or label-size guard.

## Source quotations — current text to preserve or amend

These are quotations of the current source, not claims that the selected amendments have already landed. The selected changes and the queued limits remain as recorded above.

`STA-17` (03-state-and-recovery.md:1143):

> Replace's machine-migration MUST move the machine component to the machine's new index and
> carry its installation ordinal `n` with it (`STG-20`).

`STG-20` (06-first-stage.md:643):

> `n` is the journal's installation ordinal in decimal without leading zeros, starting at zero
> per machine. It is derived from the journal with no new journal field, unchanged across restart
> and Restore.

`STG-20` (06-first-stage.md:553):

> That separately approved destructive reinstall
> opens a new installation when it is **dispatched**: the reset into rescue on a dedicated server,
> or the vendor's reinstall call at LNVPS. Choosing it or recording its disposition does not move
> that boundary. At dispatch the old installed-system pin retires and the new `ready_to_reset` job
> read can establish its pin before the reset into the installed system. Any other rescue reset,
> reboot, restart, Restore or non-destructive key recovery does not open that boundary.

`credential format v1` (docs/design/credential-format-v1.md:225):

> Missing
> or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history. `STA-16` owns what Restore does with
> these facts. These fields remain required in the version-4 payload and in the version-3
> compatibility input; the envelope and derivation are unchanged.

`ARC-43` (01-architecture.md:306):

> - `replace_root_label` — a harness-initiated rewrite of a dedicated machine's root label
>   during Replace's model-free direct re-entry migration, outside any session. The model
>   MUST NOT request it through `request_harness_job` or supply its command. Its rules are
>   `STA-17`'s.

## Owner decision — later reinstall admission over an accepted-but-incomplete history, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route with no admissible saved history, whose installation number was accepted as a proposal under the recorded decision B (for example, 7, with installations 0 to 6 unknown). Later, a separately authorized destructive reinstall opens the next installation, and its `ready_to_reset` pin comes up for admission.

Selected admission A, as an amendment: the admission compares the pin against every fact the harness retains, from the accepted installation onward. Any known overlap refuses, as now. The earlier history is shown plainly as unknown, and that comparison is never reported, displayed or exported as passed. The guard does not refuse merely because the earlier facts are unavailable.

This amends the scope of `STG-20`'s "MUST share no fingerprint with any observation or installed-system pin of that machine in any earlier installation" for this case only. For installations below the accepted base, the check covers what is retained rather than what happened. It is a relaxation, and the owner accepts it: the cost is that a stale key from the unknown installations would go undetected. `STG-20`'s backstop is already "vacuous for a predecessor that never reached `ready_to_reset` and left no matching observation", but losing a record does not prove that case, so this decision is needed.

This later owner choice sets aside two limits of the recorded decision B on this bead, for this one `STG-20` earlier-installation check on the dedicated Robot recovery path only. Decision B says "Exact partial-history comparison/admission cases and formal coverage must be resolved without assuming lost history is empty or weakening a property." and "No theorem, requirement, assumption boundary, import refusal or control may be weakened to accommodate the amendment." Everything else in decision B stands, and lost history is still never assumed empty.

Decision B also says "It does not authorize future operations whose required facts or comparisons remain unavailable." That sentence is not set aside, and it does not bar this admission. In decision B's paragraph, "It" is the versioned partial-history representation, which "must round-trip the proposal's basis and the missing past". The sentence says that this representation supplies no authority: it withholds authority rather than forbidding an operation. The authority for this admission is this owner decision. Under this decision's amended `STG-20` scope, the comparison this admission requires is the one over the retained facts, so no required comparison is unavailable.

Limits:
- Only the dedicated Robot recovery path that decision B covers. No generalized admission route follows.
- At LNVPS, `STG-21a`'s publication-based reinstall confirmation still "requires a complete nonempty publication durably recorded for the immediately preceding installation before dispatch", and `CHN-R7` admission is unchanged.
- Unknown history never becomes empty history, and every retained check, hold and no-retry rule stays.

Not selected:
- Admission B, refusing the admission whenever the required comparison includes unavailable history. That would leave the machine with no reset into the installed system after any later destructive reinstall, so its only exits would be abandonment or staying in rescue.
- Reading admission A as no relaxation, on the view that `STG-20` already covers only the history that was kept.

The independent readings split two to one. Two favored admission A; the third favored admission B and reads admission A as a relaxation of `STG-20`, which the owner accepted.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Technical common fact — genuine history below the accepted base is kept, 2026-11-03

Scope: the recorded decision B on this bead. A machine is recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route with no admissible saved history, and the operator accepts a proposed installation number, for example 7. Some genuine facts below 7 survive and are admissible under the existing rules, such as an observation known to belong to installation 4 or a retired installed pin from installation 5.

Three independent readings agree on these facts, and none calls them a new policy or an amendment:

- Each such fact is preserved in decision B's versioned partial-history representation, and the gaps around it are shown explicitly as unknown. Dropping the facts is not open: decision B says "Every retained identity, ordinal, installation observation and pin fact must be preserved". Filling the gaps is not open either: the credential format says "Missing or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history".
- `STA-16`'s Restore rule points the same way for recorded facts: it "MUST retain every recorded installation boundary, its publication observations, and each installed pin's active or retired status".
- The later-admission decision on this bead compares a later `ready_to_reset` pin against every fact the harness retains. Its phrase "from the accepted installation onward" is not a lower bound: retained facts below the accepted base join that comparison too. That makes the check stricter, never weaker, and any known overlap still refuses.
- The credential format's validation of its older versions is unchanged, including its refusal of a "duplicate or skipped installation ordinal". How the partial-history form encodes its gaps is left to the text work under decision B, and no field names are chosen here. One reading calls that encoding a technical omission owned by the credential format, coordinated with its recovery semantics.

This adds nothing beyond decision B and the later-admission decision. How decision B's "no admissible saved history" trigger applies where admissible facts reach only an earlier installation stays queued for the text work. So does whether the only partial shape admissible today is known history from the first installation onward, then a gap, then the accepted base. A single reading raised each point, and neither changes these facts.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Technical common fact — the ordinary session after a partial sheetless recovery, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered under decision B on this bead, with an accepted installation number and earlier history explicitly unknown, is handed to an ordinary session.

Three independent readings agree on these facts, and none calls them a new policy or an amendment:

- The route is `SEC-1`'s re-entry, which binds "on a maintained machine only". `SEC-1` says "Binding is an operator act in the browser, made before any channel access to that machine."
- `STA-13`'s conservative binding, under which "re-entry then binds only a configured model not currently assigned to any other machine", restricts no current tenant. `STA-11` says the ledger's staleness rules "bind only a tenant that is both maintained and threshold-bearing, and none currently is".
- Known exposure is counted. Unknown past exposure is shown as unknown, never as zero.
- The session may rely on an independently admitted active pin, and on the accepted installation number as a proposal with its recorded basis.
- The session may not rely on prior provenance, retired pins, the unknown history, zero exposure, complete revocation or a passed comparison over the unknown installations. Every ordinary check still applies. Whether `ARC-25a`'s command filter is one of them for this machine is an open owner question, below.

Single readings raised further points. Each stays queued and unchosen, and none changes these facts.

Two open owner questions, neither answered here:
- Whether `ARC-25a`'s command filter applies to a machine whose earlier history is unknown under decision B. The filter applies "For every box-plane command targeting a machine with durable unpinned-installation history", and this record does not decide whether unknown history counts as such history.
- Which machine id a bound session sees before the operator confirms the machine's label, and whether an ordinary session may bind before that confirmation.

Four points for the text work:
- Which text supplies the duty to show unknown past exposure as unknown on this route: decision B on this bead with `SEC-1`, or `STA-13`.
- Whether the rescue flow must be named in `SEC-1`, which says "Two harness flows hold a client key outside any session", and in `SEC-5` row 1, or folded into Replace.
- Whether the credential format's per-machine `installation` field, which takes `"pinned"`, `"unpinned"` or `"not_installed"`, needs an explicit unknown value.
- Whether this route needs a pointer to `STA-16`'s unchecked rule, which is worded for a sheet: "The sheet carries no check result and no finding".

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a valid late sheet enriches the live partial history, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route under the recorded decision B, whose proposed installation number was accepted (for example, 7, with earlier history unknown). Later, the operator supplies an old recovery sheet for this machine that is admissible under the existing import rules. Today no act joins a sheet's history to a store that already holds the machine.

Selected: checked, evidence-only enrichment, as an amendment. The sheet's compatible facts join the live partial history; any contradiction refuses the enrichment.

Checked means:
- The sheet passes the existing import validation under its own seed: `STA-22b`'s "Import checks the seed identifier, derives each listed public key and compares it", and the credential format's checks, are unchanged. A sheet that fails them stays outside the store, even if it would fill a gap.
- The physical machine is established by seed identifier, vendor machine id and vendor reconciliation, never by label text. Decision B already says "No label component establishes an old seed-derived identity". A different seed lineage is validated under its own seed, and its link to this machine is established separately.
- Every sheet fact is compared with every fact the harness retains before any of it joins.

Evidence-only means:
- The joined facts keep their own provenance and stay "knowledge as of export", as `STA-16` says of a restored sheet. A sheet whose last group is 5 is not a claim that the machine is at 5 today: nothing rolls back, installation 6 stays unknown, and the accepted 7 stays a proposal.
- They join every later admission comparison, as the later-admission decision on this bead and the common fact on genuine history below the accepted base already require for retained facts. A later pin that repeats a fingerprint recovered from the sheet refuses.
- They grant no binding, pin activation, contact, allocation, key removal or relabel authority. The credential format's "imported data never creates a binding without vendor reconciliation and an operator act" stands, and so does `CHN-R7`'s "Without a reinstall, no installed-system pin from any source replaces an active pin".
- The enriched history never becomes proof that it is complete or current. Gaps the sheet does not cover stay unknown, and the credential format's "Never merge two counters and call the result proof that a backup is current" applies.

Any contradiction refuses: if a sheet fact conflicts with the retained history (for example, an installation above the accepted 7 recorded before that acceptance, a second installed pin in one group, or a fingerprint that the retained history places in a different installation), the enrichment is refused. The owner selected that compatible facts join and that any contradiction refuses. This record reads the refusal as covering the whole sheet, so none of its facts join, not only the conflicting ones. The later decisions on a refused sheet were put to the owner on that reading, and the owner did not challenge it, but the owner has not confirmed it explicitly. Nothing in the live history is overwritten, renumbered or reported as passed, and decision B's "acceptance cannot override a contradiction" holds. What the conflict then means for the recovery, and for a pin admitted before it surfaced, is a separate question that stays open.

This amends `STA-16`, which gains a late-evidence act next to Restore; the credential format owns its representation. No field names are chosen here.

Not selected: no new act, which is simplest. The sheet would stay outside this store, and later comparisons could not use facts the harness had a way to know: a reinstall presenting a fingerprint the sheet records in installation 5 would be admitted with that history shown as unknown.

All three independent readings favored enrichment. Two read it as a new policy needing an amendment, and the third as a technical omission owned by `STA-16`. The owner records it as an amendment.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a late sheet that contradicts the accepted installation number, 2026-11-03

Scope: the late-sheet case on this bead. The installation number was accepted as a proposal under the recorded decision B (for example, 7), and later the operator supplies an old recovery sheet that passes the existing import checks but contradicts that number: for example, it proves installation 9 existed before 7 was accepted. Under the late-sheet enrichment record's reading of its refusal, the whole sheet is refused, so none of its facts join the live history. This record decides what the conflict then means for the recovery.

Selected K, as an amendment:
- Before the relabel write, the migration stops as the changed-label A decision already says: "stop this bounded migration unfinished and preserve the discrepancy". No relabel intent or label write is issued, the acceptance and every existing association stay under 7, and the recovery adopts no 9 and must "invent no installation boundary".
- After the write (for example, a confirmed `b-7`), the machine keeps 7. The conflict is recorded durably beside the history, never as installation facts in it, and it is shown before each irreversible step on this machine. Showing it adds no refusal of its own: every existing check, hold and no-retry rule still applies.
- The next destructive reinstall opens installation 8 and writes `b-8`. Nothing renumbers the history automatically, and no repair step is added.
- The accepted 7 stays a proposal, and the conflict is never reported as resolved or as a passed comparison. Decision B's "acceptance cannot override a contradiction" holds: the conflict stays recorded and shown and is never cleared by the acceptance.

Because the sheet's groups stay apart, the live history keeps one sequence, and the credential format's refusal of a "duplicate or skipped installation ordinal" is unchanged.

Accepted cost: the refused sheet's fingerprints do not join the history, so a later reinstall cannot be checked against them. That earlier history is shown as unknown under the later-admission decision on this bead, and that comparison is never reported as passed.

Not selected:
- Stop: halt every step that depends on history, such as the label write and later reinstalls, keeping the conflict on record with no repair. Without a repair step, this could leave the machine with no reinstall route short of abandonment.
- Repair: a new operator step that renumbers the history with evidence, for example to `b-9` and then `b-10`.

Two independent readings recommended stopping; the third recommended K and called it simplest. One of the readings that recommended stopping called stopping the simplest. None recommended repair, and none wanted automatic renumbering. Two read the effect of a late contradiction on a completed recovery as a new policy; the third said that the treatment of a newly found contradiction needs an owner decision.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a refused late sheet that overlaps the admitted pin, 2026-11-03

Scope: the late-sheet case on this bead. A machine recovered under the recorded decision B has an installed-system pin that was admitted under the existing rules, for example pin P for installation 8. Later, the operator supplies an old recovery sheet that passes the existing import checks and records the same fingerprint P in an earlier installation, such as 4. The retained history places P in a different installation, so under the late-sheet enrichment decision this is a contradiction, and under that record's reading of its refusal the whole sheet is refused.

Selected: keep the admitted pin and warn, as an amendment.
- The admitted pin stays in use. Nothing retires or replaces it automatically, consistent with `CHN-R7`'s "Without a reinstall, no installed-system pin from any source replaces an active pin".
- The overlap is recorded durably beside the history, never as installation facts in it, and it is shown before each irreversible step on this machine, as the selected keep-and-record decision K for a contradicted installation number does. Showing it adds no refusal of its own: every existing check, hold and no-retry rule still applies.
- The overlap is never reported as resolved, and no comparison it touches is reported as passed. Decision B's "acceptance cannot override a contradiction" holds.
- A later destructive reinstall still opens a new installation with a new pin under the existing admission rules, which ends this pin's use in the ordinary way.

The credential format already says, within one installation, that later refused observations "MUST NOT invalidate an already admitted pin". This decision gives a refused late sheet the same effect on a pin it challenges across installations. It does not change that rule or the format's validation.

Accepted cost: contact continues on a pin whose freshness against earlier installations is now challenged. Because the refused sheet's facts do not join the history, later admission checks cannot use them either.

Not selected: suspend contact that relies on the pin until the conflict is reconciled. No step reconciles the overlap: none is defined, and decision K on this bead did not select repair. Suspension would therefore last until a destructive reinstall gave the machine a new pin or the machine was abandoned.

Two independent readings recommended keeping the pin, and the third recommended suspending contact. All three called keeping it the simplest.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — an ordinary session before the rescue relabel is confirmed, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered under decision B on this bead, without a recovery sheet, whose relabel to the new id (for example, `b-7`) has not been confirmed by a captured readback. This answers the second open owner question in the common-fact record on this bead titled "Technical common fact — the ordinary session after a partial sheetless recovery": which machine id a bound session sees in that window, and whether an ordinary session may bind before confirmation. Decision B already says "Confirmed label/current-ID status needs the captured installed-system readback following the selected new-key login", and that `b-7` is shown "as the proposed or pending destination after acceptance".

Selected, as an amendment:
- While the bounded recovery flow runs, no ordinary session binds the machine, as in Replace's flow, which runs "in a model-free harness flow — no session is bound and no model sees either key".
- Once that flow has stopped unfinished, for example after the changed-label A stop, the operator may bind an ordinary session through `SEC-1`'s re-entry, which binds "on a maintained machine only".
- The model is shown the pending id, for example `b-7`, marked unconfirmed, with each label the harness has read from the disk beside it as an as-of observation. Decision B already says that once a write has been sent, the earlier observed `a-7` "is only an as-of observation, not an assertion about the disk's current label". No observed label becomes the machine's id: "A disk label is never adopted automatically", and changed-label A still holds: "adopt no `9` and invent no installation boundary".
- In the install brief, on a machine whose relabel is unconfirmed, a root whose label does not equal the shown id is surfaced to the operator. It is never erased as the predecessor, and never resumed or treated as found complete, until a destructive reinstall of this machine is dispatched. This narrows, for this window only, the brief's rule that "An unmarked or foreign-id root is the approved predecessor, not a resume".
- At that dispatch the boundary moves as `STG-20` already says: the separately approved destructive reinstall "opens a new installation when it is **dispatched**". Decision B already says that "a later separately approved and otherwise admissible destructive reinstall derives 8 at its existing dispatch boundary while retaining the unknown past".

This keeps a reinstall route open after a stop. The owner decision on this bead titled "Owner decision — a late sheet that contradicts the accepted installation number" did not select Stop because it "could leave the machine with no reinstall route short of abandonment", and the one titled "Owner decision — later reinstall admission over an accepted-but-incomplete history" did not select admission B because "its only exits would be abandonment or staying in rescue". A dedicated reinstall needs a session: a reinstall approval is "bound to its reset call, entry, approved facts and the session it was rendered for", and `SEC-4` says "A typed operation that names an existing machine MUST be authorized against the calling session's binding".

Not selected:
- No ordinary session until a read shows the new id. This was the simplest option, but after a changed-label stop no session could bind, so no reinstall could be approved either.
- Bind, and have the install brief also accept the observed labels as this installation's. A changed label such as `a-9` would then have to be treated either as this installation, against changed-label A, or as foreign, which the brief treats as "the approved predecessor".
- Show the observed label as the current id. Decision B says "No label component establishes an old seed-derived identity".

Two independent readings recommended no ordinary session until a read shows the new id; the third recommended the selected option. All three called the no-session option the simplest, and all three called the policy for the stopped branches new and an amendment. One held that no ordinary session binding while the flow runs is already required by the source. None recommended accepting the observed labels as this installation's.

The readings also corrected the question as it was put to them:
- No source text reserves formatting to an approved reinstall. `STG-20` says "The label steers the model; nothing checks it", and ADR-0045 says "No label check, disk record or cross-module dependency is introduced."
- An approved destructive reinstall is not the hazard: at its dispatch a new installation opens and the old root is the predecessor erased "as approved for this install".
- The hazard is a return to rescue without a destructive reinstall. `CNF-86` exercises that return after a confirmed relabel, where it "finds one root whose label equals the shown id". Before confirmation the one root can carry another label, and neither of the brief's existing stops applies: "An unresolved label probe or two roots carrying the current id means stop and surface, never erase."
- An install unfinished in rescue is not a Resume case for Replace, which "refuses to migrate an install unfinished in rescue".

Text work named by the readings. Each holds whichever way the current text is read on the shown id in this window, either as the pending id from acceptance, since `STA-22b` says to reserve the machine index "durably before any external effect", or as no defined current id:
- A rescue-path counterpart to `STA-17`'s rule that the shown id moves "never before the disk does", which today applies "In this direct re-entry".
- A rescue-path counterpart to `STA-17`'s re-read rule, "Until a read of the label succeeds, the harness MUST re-read it on each later connection to the machine", which today follows "In that flow".
- Whether to name the rescue flow in `SEC-1`, which says "Two harness flows hold a client key outside any session", and in `SEC-5` row 1, or to fold it into Replace, a point already listed for the text work in that common-fact record.
- The install brief itself, for this window: Step 1's "An unmarked root, another installation's id or another machine's id is the predecessor, including a hand-installed root. It is erased on the selected disks as approved for this install", Step 3's "With only a predecessor, or no root, on the approved disks, partition and format as approved below" and its Resume rule, "An unmarked or foreign-id root is the approved predecessor, not a resume". The same rule is restated in ADR-0045, "an unmarked or foreign root is the predecessor, including a hand-installed one", and in `CNF-86 · BLOCKING`, "A fresh reinstall erases the approved predecessor, including an unmarked, foreign-id or hand-installed root". Each is checked against this window, in which a surfaced root is erased only once a destructive reinstall of this machine is dispatched.
- Conformance cases for the stopped branches beside `CNF-20`'s relabel cases, and an install-brief case for the surfaced root.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — the command filter on a machine whose installation history is unknown, 2026-11-03

Scope: a machine recovered under decision B on this bead, where "Earlier installation history remains explicitly unknown." This answers the first open owner question in the common-fact record on this bead titled "Technical common fact — the ordinary session after a partial sheetless recovery": "Whether `ARC-25a`'s command filter applies to a machine whose earlier history is unknown under decision B." That record left it open: the filter applies "For every box-plane command targeting a machine with durable unpinned-installation history", and the record "does not decide whether unknown history counts as such history".

Selected, as a new policy and an amendment:
- On such a machine, the explicit unknown that decision B's recovery records for installation history triggers `ARC-25a`'s filter, as durable unpinned-installation history does. The filter itself is unchanged: "A match MUST prevent transmission and command-intent creation."
- The trigger is that recorded unknown and nothing broader. Absence of contrary evidence, or history that is merely incomplete, does not fire this trigger. An ordinary Restore of a sheet that carries no such recorded unknown is not caught by this trigger: its installation facts "are restored and shown beside it, as of export like the rest". Where those restored facts record an unpinned installation, the filter applies as `ARC-25a` already says, for a machine "with durable unpinned-installation history". The legacy decision on `tw-l1l`, which applies the filter to "every machine that could be the origin of the unpinned history", is unchanged.
- The filter stays on after a later pinned reinstall. Such a reinstall "opens a new installation when it is **dispatched**" (`STG-20`), and decision B already derives the next ordinal "while retaining the unknown past". A pinned successor does not resolve the unknown.
- Refusals and the trust display say unknown, never unpinned. `ARC-25a` requires one refusal "containing the target and form", and "Replay preserves the recorded refusal and its target qualification": that qualification is unknown history. What the display discloses beside the unknown history is left to the `ARC-25a` text work below. It does not assert that any installation ran unpinned.
- This decision adds no way to clear the unknown or to lift the filter. The legacy decision on `tw-l1l` left resolving the uncertainty from a matching journal backup as "a separate queued proposal, not selected by A". The queued follow-up notes after it, in the section titled "Queued follow-up notes — not decisions", warn "do not assume a match alone authorizes clearing unknown or lifting a filter". That proposal stays queued and is not extended here.

The legacy decision on `tw-l1l` (ambiguous legacy installation history, 2026-11-02) is a precedent for this tradeoff, not its authority. That decision chose to "Apply the existing ARC-25a command filter to every machine that could be the origin of the unpinned history", and accepted that "Some commands may consequently be refused on a machine that was never unpinned". It covered a backup that "preserves an unpinned predecessor on the set {M, N} but cannot identify the originating machine". There, an unpinned installation is known and only its machine is uncertain. Here, no unpinned installation is known. The technical settlement on that thread titled "Technical settlement — T47 source pruning and successor authority" limits its reach: "The explicit-unknown decision already selected for ambiguous unpinned-installation origins is not automatically extended to those other facts". Those other facts are missing legacy jump-vendor, date and account-statement data. This decision extends the filter choice to decision B's unknown installation history by owner choice, and extends nothing to those other facts.

The filter stays a narrow guard. It "does not evaluate shell or establish effective package policy", other forms "can evade the filter", and "Harmless matching text is refused". It cannot block the recovery flow itself: "No command text the harness composes contains a literal lowering form".

Not selected:
- Leaving the trigger as written, so that unknown history alone does not fire the filter. This was the simplest option. The example that separates it from the selected option is a command such as `sed -i 's/^SigLevel.*/SigLevel = Never/' /etc/pacman.conf`. Under this option it goes on to the other admissions, even though the running installation may be unpinned.
- Filtering only while the running installation's status is unknown, and lifting the filter after a recorded pinned reinstall. Lifting would end the filter while the earlier history is still unknown.

All three independent readings recommended the selected option and called leaving the trigger as written the simplest. All three called the selected option a new policy and an amendment, and none read it as already required by the source. Each reading also raised the lifting variant, and none recommended it.

The readings also corrected the question as it was put to them:
- "Missing history is never converted into empty history" is in the legacy decision on `tw-l1l`, not in decision B. Decision B's sentence is that acceptance cannot "convert a missing comparison into a passed comparison". Neither sentence forces this choice. Nor does the credential format's "Missing or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history": each governs how history and comparisons are represented, and the trigger compares nothing.
- The filter does not refuse any bytes that contain a lowering form. It works line by line: "Split raw bytes at LF." It skips comment lines: "Ignore lines whose first non-whitespace byte is `#`." A `SigLevel`-family word "followed later on that line by `=` opens a suffix through line end", in which a `Never`-family or `TrustAll`-family word selects the form.
- The question assumed a pinned running installation over an unknown past. The readings split on whether the running installation's own pin status is unknown after this recovery. One reading held that it is. Two said this cannot be told from the text, since an independent admissible record could establish it. This decision does not choose between them, and the point stays queued with the representation work below.

Text work, for the text that implements decision B:
- `ARC-25a`: the trigger, the refusal's target qualification and the display beside unknown history, including which of the disclosures it gives "Beside **unpinned**" apply there. Its package-signature disclosure describes the unpinned baseline, not a pinned reinstall.
- The recovery representation in `STA-16` and the credential format, already open in that common-fact record, which asks whether the credential format's per-machine `installation` field "needs an explicit unknown value". The trigger must key on the explicit unknown that decision B's recovery records for installation history, however that work represents it. Whether the running installation's own unrecorded status is part of that unknown is an open, unchosen question for that work.
- `SEC-14`'s restatement, under which the machine's history is shown to "every later set that includes the machine" at binding.
- Conformance cases: refusal of harmless matching text on a machine with unknown history; the filter still on after a recorded pinned reinstall; and an ordinary sheet Restore whose recorded history holds no unpinned installation and no explicit unknown, which this trigger does not catch.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — a late sheet stays outside the store, 2026-11-04

Scope: the late-sheet case on this bead. A machine was recovered through the dedicated Robot rescue route under the recorded decision B, and its proposed installation number was accepted (for example, 7, with earlier history unknown). Later, the operator finds an old recovery sheet for this machine.

Selected, as an amendment of the owner's own earlier late-sheet decisions on this bead: no late-sheet act. A found sheet stays outside the store, as the enrichment record below says it does today: "no act joins a sheet's history to a store that already holds the machine". None of its facts join the live history, and none are kept for later comparison. The earlier history stays shown as unknown under the later-admission decision on this bead, and that comparison is never reported as passed.

This withdraws three owner decisions on this bead, all dated 2026-11-03, and one open point:
- "Owner decision — a valid late sheet enriches the live partial history". `STA-16` gains no late-evidence act, and the credential format gains no representation for one.
- "Owner decision — a late sheet that contradicts the accepted installation number" (decision K). Its before-write stop restated the changed-label A decision. Changed-label A is triggered by the disk's label, not by a sheet, and stands unchanged.
- "Owner decision — a refused late sheet that overlaps the admitted pin". No sheet is refused, because none is taken in. An admitted pin is governed by the existing rules alone, including `CHN-R7`'s "Without a reinstall, no installed-system pin from any source replaces an active pin".
- Whether the enrichment refusal covers the whole sheet. The enrichment record read it that way and said the owner had not confirmed it explicitly. With no enrichment there is no refusal to cover.

Unchanged: decision B; the later-admission decision; the common fact on genuine history below the accepted base, which concerns facts the harness retains at recovery, not a later sheet; the decision on an ordinary session before the rescue relabel is confirmed; and the decision on the command filter for unknown history. The ordinary-session decision cites decision K's reason for not selecting Stop. That citation records why its options were weighed and does not depend on K staying selected.

Accepted cost: the cost the enrichment record named for its own "no new act" option. A reinstall presenting a fingerprint that the found sheet records in an earlier installation is admitted, with that history shown as unknown. A found sheet that records an unpinned earlier installation does not give the machine "durable unpinned-installation history" either, so `ARC-25a`'s filter does not fire on that sheet. Whether the filter fires on the recorded unknown is the command-filter decision on this bead.

Not selected:
- Keep only the found sheet's checked fingerprints, with no merge into the live history, so that a later reinstall repeating one of them is refused.
- Keep the three withdrawn decisions as recorded.

Five independent readings judged whether the system needs the late-sheet decisions. Four recommended against keeping them as recorded: two recommended this option, and two recommended keeping only the fingerprints. The fifth recommended keeping them as recorded. The owner chose this option over the two-to-two tie, knowingly amending the owner's own earlier picks. It weakens no current text: none of the withdrawn decisions had reached the normative text.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Owner decision — the restart, changed-label and old-key decisions after the need review, 2026-11-04

Scope: three decisions in the record on this bead titled "Owner decision — rescue ordinal accepted as a proposal, 2026-11-02" (comment 37000001): follow-up A (the acceptance survives a worker restart), changed-label A, and old-key A. Five independent readings judged whether the system needs each of them. The owner selected the recommendation on each, as voted.

Follow-up A, the restart: the behavior stands, and the later text work adds no restart clause of its own. The durable ordinal acceptance is an ordinary journaled record under `STA-3` ("If the append fails, the transition does not occur"), bound to the same machine, root and destination allocation, and resuming the unchanged recorded migration reads it back from the journal. The limits in follow-up A stand and come from the existing rules: no revived worker authority, no different target or changed proposal, no automatic retry (`STA-6`; for the label write, `STA-17` says re-issuing it "MUST be a fresh issue the operator chooses in Replace's flow, never an automatic retry"), and no claim that a possibly sent write completed. Three readings recommended this mechanism; two recommended keeping follow-up A as recorded, with the same behavior.

Changed-label A stands as recorded: a changed label observed on the same recorded root before the relabel write stops the migration unfinished, and it adds no mandatory pre-write probe. Three readings recommended keeping it as recorded. Two recommended simplifying it: one by merging it with the late-sheet conflict rules, which the late-sheet decision on this bead (comment 72000001) has since withdrawn, and one by a compare-and-set inside the relabel job. Neither simplification is selected.

Old-key A stands as recorded: only the exact old public key that checked retained machine records identify is removed, after the new-key login and the confirmed `b-7` readback; unknown keys stay untouched and revocation is reported incomplete. Four readings recommended keeping it as recorded. One recommended rewriting `authorized_keys` to the new key alone after the login and readback; that whole-file option stays queued and unchosen, as old-key A recorded it.

Open for the later text work: when the old key cannot be identified, old-key A leaves it in place, and BLOCKING `CNF-5` reads "only that machine's public key appears in its `authorized_keys`". The text work must reconcile old-key A with `CNF-5` and must not weaken `CNF-5` to do so. `STA-17`'s direct Replace already leaves an old key in place on a failed confirmation ("a failed confirmation leaves the old key in place") and never reports complete revocation while it remains outstanding. This record does not choose how the two are reconciled.

Unchanged: decision B, job-order A, the later-admission decision, the ordinary-session decision, and the late-sheet decision.

This record makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

## Agent Brief — bounded specification amendment, the dedicated rescue rekey's ordinal, relabel and partial history

**Category:** bug. **Outcome:** land, in their normative homes, the owner decisions and technical common facts already recorded on this bead. No further owner choice is needed for the scope below. Points the owner left unchosen stay unchosen: where the text work would have to choose one, stop and report it instead of choosing. The bead moves to ready-for-agent with this brief; the drain lane takes it after its current queue.

This bead's description is the question as filed, and it says the gap must be settled before a dedicated-server path is offered, "which no stage before the third does". Stages are removed (tw-o6r). The governing admission row is "The dedicated path: the construction test bed" in `07-conformance.md`, whose cases, item 84's Robot rescue case and item 20's relabel cases included, pass on the integrated harness "before a dedicated-server path is offered to an operator". This brief governs the text work.

**Records this brief implements (sections on this bead, by title).** Each section's own text, limits and "Not selected" list govern. This brief summarizes them and widens none.

- "Owner decision — rescue ordinal accepted as a proposal, 2026-11-02" (decision B), with its follow-up A, job-order A, display timing, changed-label A and old-key A.
- "Owner decision — later reinstall admission over an accepted-but-incomplete history, 2026-11-03" (admission A).
- "Technical common fact — genuine history below the accepted base is kept, 2026-11-03".
- "Technical common fact — the ordinary session after a partial sheetless recovery, 2026-11-03". Both of its open owner questions are closed: the second by the ordinary-session decision below, the first by the filter removal ("Scope of the filter withdrawal, 2026-11-04").
- "Owner decision — an ordinary session before the rescue relabel is confirmed, 2026-11-03".
- "Owner decision — the command filter on a machine whose installation history is unknown, 2026-11-03", only the points that "Scope of the filter withdrawal, 2026-11-04" keeps standing.
- "Owner decision — a late sheet stays outside the store, 2026-11-04".
- "Owner decision — the restart, changed-label and old-key decisions after the need review, 2026-11-04".

Withdrawn, and implemented by none of this brief: the three late-sheet decisions of 2026-11-03 ("Owner decision — a valid late sheet enriches the live partial history", "Owner decision — a late sheet that contradicts the accepted installation number" (K) and "Owner decision — a refused late sheet that overlaps the admitted pin"), withdrawn by the 2026-11-04 late-sheet decision; and the filter parts of the command-filter decision (its trigger, the filter staying on after a pinned reinstall, the refusal's target qualification and its conformance cases), withdrawn by "Owner direction — the command filter is removed, and C8 is moot, 2026-11-04" as scoped by "Scope of the filter withdrawal, 2026-11-04".

**Current gap.** `STA-17`'s relabel applies "In this direct re-entry", and `ARC-43`'s `replace_root_label` runs "during Replace's model-free direct re-entry migration". The rescue recovery that `STA-22b` describes moves the machine to a fresh-seed index with no relabel, no defined ordinal `n` and no rule for when the machine counts as migrated. No representation carries a history whose earlier installations are unknown, and the credential format says "Missing or invalid history MUST NOT become empty history". `STG-20`'s reinstall admission "MUST share no fingerprint with any observation or installed-system pin of that machine in any earlier installation", which such a history cannot show. The install brief treats a root whose label differs from the shown id as the predecessor, so a return to rescue before confirmation can steer toward erasing the machine's own root.

**Desired behavior and owners.** Normative owners are `STA-17`, `STG-20`, `STA-16` and the credential format, with `ARC-43` for the job and the install brief for the surfaced root; decision B places the rationale with ADR-0045. Change the single owners together, then record the amendment.

- **The ordinal, decision B**, at `STA-17` and `STG-20`. During authorized rescue recovery of the same physical maintained machine, with no admissible saved history and a unique disk label such as `a-7`, the operator may explicitly accept 7 as a proposed current installation ordinal after checks against surviving facts; migration to new index b uses `b-7`. A disk label is never adopted automatically, and no label component establishes an old seed-derived identity. The number is a proposal, never historical proof. Earlier history stays explicitly unknown; known history carries forward; every retained identity, ordinal, observation and pin fact is preserved. Acceptance cannot override a contradiction or turn a missing comparison into a passed one. Reading or accepting a label opens no destructive installation, establishes no prior pin provenance, authenticates no root contents, identifies no old client key, revokes nothing and completes no Replace. The base does not increment during non-destructive recovery; a later separately approved, otherwise admissible destructive reinstall derives 8 at its existing dispatch boundary, retaining the unknown past and waiving no guard.
- **The partial-history representation**, at the credential format (a new version) and `STA-16`. It round-trips the proposal's basis and the missing past without turning either into ordinary recovered history. Old-version validation is unchanged, its refusal of a "duplicate or skipped installation ordinal" included; fabricate no earlier groups, observations, pins or empty-history placeholders. The compact export carries its own interpretable acceptance basis and unknown-history meaning; a pointer to missing journal evidence is not enough. Genuine admissible facts below the accepted base are preserved, with the gaps around them shown as unknown. Keep the captured observation and root provenance, the target-bound operator act, retained facts, relabel intent and result, and captured confirmation as separate linked facts. A failed acceptance append supplies no acceptance. The representation supplies no authority for later operations. No field names are chosen.
- **Restart.** The acceptance is an ordinary journaled record under `STA-3` ("If the append fails, the transition does not occur"), bound to the same machine, root and destination allocation; resuming the unchanged recorded migration reads it back. Add no restart clause of its own. Its limits come from existing rules: no revived worker authority, no different target or changed proposal, no automatic retry (`STA-6`, and `STA-17`'s "MUST be a fresh issue the operator chooses in Replace's flow, never an automatic retry"), and no claim that a possibly sent write completed.
- **The job and its order, job-order A**, at `STA-17` and `ARC-43`'s job list, which today has no rescue rekey job. Write the root label and read it back only after the installed system accepts a login authenticated with the new client key. The bounded harness job runs in the installed system. A failed new-key login leaves `a-7` untouched. A pinned host answer or rescue authentication is not installed-system acceptance of the key. Keep the relabel's captured readback distinct from installed access, old-key revocation and whole Replace completion. Give the rescue path counterparts of `STA-17`'s "never before the disk does" and of "Until a read of the label succeeds, the harness MUST re-read it on each later connection to the machine".
- **Display.** After acceptance, show `b-7` as the proposed or pending destination, and distinguish allocation `b`, observed disk text `a-7`, installed access and label confirmation. Confirmed label and current-id status need the captured installed-system readback after the new-key login. Once a write is sent, the observed `a-7` is only an as-of observation. Label confirmation, terminal job evidence, hold release and revocation stay separate facts.
- **A changed label, changed-label A.** If an admissible captured observation of the same recorded root reports a changed label (such as `a-9`) before the relabel write, stop this bounded migration unfinished and preserve the discrepancy. Issue no relabel intent or write. Retain the acceptance, both observations, the allocation and every association under 7; adopt no 9 and invent no installation boundary. The earlier new-key installation is not undone. The stop creates no command hold without a sent command, grants no erasure and implies no cleanup or revocation. Add no mandatory pre-write probe. Restart does not normalize the discrepancy into success.
- **The old key, old-key A.** The model-free flow removes only the exact old client public key that checked retained machine records for the same authorized machine identify, after the installed-system new-key login and the confirmed `b-7` readback. Preserve the new key and unrelated authorizations. Missing old private material is not missing public identity; report no impossible old-key login test as passed. Unknown keys stay untouched and revocation is reported incomplete; they supply no deletion target, no whole-file replacement and no new command hold. A removal supports only its scoped effect. The changed-label stop does not proceed to removal.
- **Later reinstall admission, admission A**, at `STG-20`, for this dedicated Robot recovery path only. A later `ready_to_reset` pin is compared against every fact the harness retains, retained facts below the accepted base included; any known overlap refuses. The earlier history is shown as unknown, and that comparison is never reported, displayed or exported as passed. The guard does not refuse merely because earlier facts are unavailable. This narrows the quoted `STG-20` check's scope for this case, as the owner accepted. At LNVPS, `STG-21a`'s confirmation still "requires a complete nonempty publication durably recorded for the immediately preceding installation before dispatch", and `CHN-R7` admission is unchanged.
- **The ordinary session.** While the bounded recovery flow runs, no ordinary session binds the machine. Once the flow has stopped unfinished, the operator may bind one through `SEC-1`'s re-entry. The model is shown the pending id marked unconfirmed, with each label read from the disk beside it as an as-of observation; no observed label becomes the id. Known exposure is counted, and unknown past exposure is shown as unknown, never zero. The session may rely on an independently admitted active pin and on the accepted number as a proposal with its basis, and on nothing the common-fact record excludes. The trust display says unknown, never unpinned, for that history, and asserts no installation ran unpinned.
- **The install brief**, at `docs/briefs/01-install.md` Step 1, Step 3 and its Resume rule ("An unmarked or foreign-id root is the approved predecessor, not a resume"), with ADR-0045's restatement and `CNF-86` checked against this window. On a machine whose relabel is unconfirmed, a root whose label does not equal the shown id is surfaced to the operator. It is never erased as the predecessor, resumed or treated as complete until a destructive reinstall of this machine is dispatched.
- **A found sheet stays outside the store.** No late-sheet act: none of its facts join the live history or are kept for later comparison, `STA-16` gains no late-evidence act, and the credential format gains no representation for one.

**Stop and report — unchosen points; choose none of them:**

- **`CNF-5`.** Where the old key cannot be identified, old-key A leaves it in place, and BLOCKING `CNF-5` reads "only that machine's public key appears in its `authorized_keys`". The text work must reconcile old-key A with `CNF-5` without weakening `CNF-5`. `STA-17`'s direct Replace already says "a failed confirmation leaves the old key in place" and never reports complete revocation while it remains. The records choose no reconciliation, and this brief chooses none: if the text forces no single answer, stop and report.
- Whether the running installation's own unrecorded status is part of the unknown. It stays open and unchosen.
- Points left to the text work, settled only where the text forces one answer:
  - how the partial form encodes its gaps, and whether the per-machine `installation` field needs an explicit unknown value;
  - how the "no admissible saved history" trigger applies where admissible facts reach only an earlier installation, and whether known history from the first installation, then a gap, then the accepted base is the only admissible partial shape;
  - which text supplies the duty to show unknown past exposure as unknown: decision B with `SEC-1`, or `STA-13`;

title: Define the single-machine session route to a different entry after definitive failure
description:
# Define the single-machine session route to a different entry after definitive failure

## Question

When the sole machine allocation of a stage-1 session definitively fails, can that same live session order a different newly approved entry? How is that consistent with retained bound-set membership and the single-machine stage-1 constraint? If it needs a successor session, what ends the old one and authorizes the new one?

## Established boundary

SEC-1 says "No machine leaves a set while the session is alive — what the model has read from it stays in the context that commands the rest."

STA-24 says "A different approved entry is independent, and creating it while a sibling is unresolved is permitted under its own approval, whose card shows the unresolved sibling and that it may be billing."

The unresolved-sibling rule supplies neither an exception to session membership nor an automatic route after definitive failure. A different entry and a new allocation index are not themselves authority to grow or shrink a single-machine session. The pending bounded repair adds no such route.

## Answer must demonstrate

- Specify the permissible stage-1 route, including old session membership, any required session end/successor, approval of the new entry and retained failed-allocation history.
- Distinguish same-entry replacement from a different entry, unresolved sibling from definitive failure, and stage-1 single-machine sessions from stage-2 set growth. Preserve any profile independence-bound constraint.
- Supply conformance refusal for an unauthorized added entry and admission for the chosen operator-approved route; a fresh index must not bypass the boundary.
- Land the answer with SEC-1/ARC-15 and the stage-1 applicability owners, updating affected formalized clauses and prose together.

No live vendor call or runtime reproduction is claimed. This is a specification question, not an implementation instruction to add automatic retries or discard a failed member.

Category: bug. State: needs-triage. Priority: P2. No behavior answer, implementation readiness or closure is implied by filing this question.
close_reason: Landed: a different approved entry replaces a never-sent machine entry in the same session, marking Failed in the same sole-writer act (STA-22b; SEC-1, SEC-4, ARC-15, STA-24, CNF-72, ADR-0037 amendment; PR #80)

## Owner decision — what makes a replacement a different intended entry, 2026-11-05

The replacement act in `STA-22b` refuses a replacement that "differs from the old entry only in its approved-entry identity, label, allocation, index, account, cost or call, which makes it the same intended entry". The question was what, beyond that list, makes a replacement a different intended entry. For example: same vendor and plan with a different region, or the same region with a different size or image.

The owner picked "Changes to the machine count". A replacement whose vendor, plan or size, region or image differs from the old entry's is a different intended entry, and the act may admit it if every other refusal clears. A replacement that differs only in its bundle commit, or in an incidental argument such as an order's reference field, together with the listed facts, is still the same intended entry. The same intended entry still has no successor.

**The counts.** Four independent readers were asked. On whether the text already forces an answer, three said it does not decide and one said it forces this reading. On the recommendation, three backed this reading and one backed a test of the entry's role or purpose. In its first wording the option took in "other approved create facts", and one reader noted that this was too broad because it covered the bundle commit and the reference field. The pick uses the narrowed wording.

**Framing corrections the text work keeps:** `STA-24`'s barrier ("While any call naming a resource is unresolved") is not what holds back the same intended entry; the refusal is `STA-22b`'s own clause (two of four). This pick decides only whether an entry is distinct. Every other refusal of the act still applies, including "when the replacement would reuse or repeat an unresolved preparation step of the old entry". Whether a step of the same kind under the replacement's new identity (for example `STG-21`'s email submission) counts as such a repeat is a separate point, not decided here (three of four readers said the text cannot tell).

**Not selected:** requiring a change of the entry's role or purpose.

title: Remove the stage plan from the specification; describe the system by capability
