title: What does the sheet hold for an old public key still awaiting removal after migration?
description:
## Why this issue exists

Found while settling `tw-rds` (comment 115000001). The credential format's version-7 text says "A migrated machine has no entry", and `STA-17` says of a dedicated machine's relabel "only after that may the old key be removed". So after an ordinary migration the machine's entry and records move to the new seed in one journal act, while its retired-seed public key is still installed and awaits removal. Nothing on the new seed's sheet records that old key. After a Restore from that sheet, the harness cannot tell that a retired public key is still on the machine or finish its removal.

The `tw-rds` pick has the same shape for a superseded reservation: the act that migrates the machine ends the reservation's entry, though its recorded key is "one more retired public key that re-entry removes".

## Question

What does the sheet hold for a migrated machine's old public key, and a superseded reservation's, until re-entry removes it? Whether this needs a sheet record, a screen statement or nothing is a real choice; the text does not force it.

## Closes when

The credential format's payload version 7 (or a later version), `STA-17` and `CNF-84` say what the sheet holds for a retired public key still installed after its machine migrated, and what a Restore from that sheet does with it, without weakening `STA-22b`'s derive-and-compare check or any existing theorem, gate, requirement or assumption.
close_reason: Text merged per comment 135000001

comments.author: user
comments.text: Scope, from the tw-rds review pass (2026-11-05): the same gap covers the read-confirmed branch of a later Replace. After a failed relabel read the machine's original retired-seed key stays installed; when the next Replace's label read shows the reserved index's id, one act confirms that migration and ends the machine's original entry, and nothing on the sheet then records that original key, whose removal is still owed. A fix may require removal before the last tracking entry ends, keep a pending entry until removal is confirmed, or state the limit on the screen; the text does not force one.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Owner pick — a pending-removal entry keeps an unremoved retired key on the sheet, 2026-11-05

The question: after Replace's migration act, a migrated machine's retired-seed public key, and any
superseded reservation's key, may still be installed until its removal is confirmed. The
credential format says "A migrated machine has no entry" and that the migration act "ends the
machine's retired-seed entry and every superseded reservation naming it", so nothing on the new
seed's sheet records that key. The same holds for the read-confirmed branch of a later Replace
(comment 116000001). What does the sheet hold, and what does a Restore do with it?

**A, accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule, 4 of 4.** "Keep a pending-removal entry
until removal is confirmed." Four independent readers answered; a fifth seat was unavailable. All
four said the text forces none of the options, and all four said B conflicts with `STA-17`'s "that
is when the shown installation id (`STG-20`) MUST move to the new index ... and only after that may
the old key be removed" unless that sentence changes.

**Replace stays reported incomplete until each removal is confirmed: yes, accepted under the same
rule, 4 of 4.** All four said the text does not say so today for a machine already migrated.

**Consequences all four gave:**
- The migration act, and a later Replace's read-confirmed act, convert the machine's retired-seed
  entry and each superseded reservation naming it into one entry per retired key not confirmed
  removed, in `retired_allocations`, with `outstanding` reason `"old_key_unremoved"` and a link to
  the machine it is installed on. It keeps its own seed, index and recorded key. It is not a second
  machine: no record names it, and it has no machine state or artifact history.
- One journal act ends it once a harness-composed read, durably appended, shows that exact key
  absent. A failed removal, a lost result or a failed append leaves it standing. The act that
  destroys the machine also ends it.
- A later migration of the machine moves each entry's link to the machine's new name in its one act.
- After a Restore, import accepts its recorded key without deriving it, under the existing one
  exception. It restores no allocation, record, contact identity or binding. The removal runs over
  a connection authenticated by the machine's own current key, removes exactly the recorded key, and
  never a current key; it needs no derive-and-compare of the recorded key from the retired seed,
  and works with or without that seed.
- `STA-17`'s "Re-entering a machine to remove the old key uses the old key" is limited to re-entry
  before migration.
- Payload version 7 is amended, as ADR-0058 and ADR-0059 did.
- No theorem or gate changes, and `STA-22b`'s derive-and-compare is not weakened.

**Narrowings and widenings the readers named:** "A migrated machine has no entry" becomes no
*machine* entry; the migration act's "ends ... every superseded reservation naming it" and
ADR-0059's "The act that migrates or destroys the machine ends its superseded reservations" narrow
on the migrate side; `retired_allocations`' "holds exactly" and `STA-22b`'s journal keep list
widen; the repeated resource-identity mappings import accepts widen to three; `STA-17`'s "uses the
old key" narrows to re-entry before migration. One reader noted that if ADR-0056's "checked
retained records" means derived and compared, removing the recorded key without the retired seed
narrows it for this removal. ADR-0053's rejected row is untouched: it concerns the LNVPS rebuild's
old machine, which never migrates.

**Detail left to the text work:** the link member's name (each reader proposed a different one);
whether the link may also name an outstanding retired machine entry, which two readers said the
read-confirmed branch needs; and which `CNF-20` and `CNF-84` cases check it.

**Not selected:** B, removal before the migration act; C, no sheet record and a screen statement
of the limit.

This pick is settled and must not be re-asked. It makes no normative edit and no capability,
readiness or runtime claim.

comments.text:
## Closed — a migrated machine's unremoved old key stays on the sheet as a pending removal, 2026-11-05

The owner's pick in comment 134000001 is now text:

- **`STA-17`.** The migration act, and a later Replace's read-confirmed act, keep the machine's old key and each superseded reservation's key as a pending removal linked to the machine's current name. The removal runs over the connection authenticated by the machine's own checked key under its existing pin and takes out exactly the recorded key. A durably appended read showing the key absent ends it; so does the act that records the machine's deletion evidence. While one stands, Replace and revocation stay reported incomplete across restart, export and Restore, and the screen names it by its machine and its key's seed. After a Restore the removal is a step of Replace's flow, with or without the seed the key was allocated under.
- **`STA-22b`.** The journal keeps a pending removal among its retired entries. Its recorded key is accepted without being derived, under the existing one exception, and is never contact authority.
- **Credential format, payload version 7.** A pending removal is a `retired_allocations` entry with reason `"old_key_unremoved"` and a `removal_of` link. It has no record, machine state or artifact history, and import refuses a malformed or misdirected link.
- **Conformance.** `CNF-20` covers the interrupted removal, a lost result, holds, and Restore with and without the seeds. `CNF-84` covers the sheet entry, the read-confirmed branch and the refusals.
- **ADR-0066** records the decision, and ADR-0059's amendment note points to it.

**Detail left to the text work.** The link is named `removal_of`, and it may name an outstanding retired machine entry while a later Replace has not yet migrated the machine. Import also refuses a link naming a reserved migration index or a machine whose own key equals the recorded key.

One review pass ran before the merge, four readers with a fifth seat unavailable, and its fixes are in. The decision narrows and widens earlier text and ADR-0059's migrate side, each listed in ADR-0066, and touches no theorem.

This closure makes no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Under an untyped vendor scope, does a destructive hold refuse harness-started jobs?
description:
`STA-24` pauses "a box-plane command to any machine of the session's bound set at that vendor" while a call under the scope is open or unresolved, and says "a continuation that continues ends the pause and a destructive one does not (*the hold*, below)"; the hold "keeps the model's box-plane commands to the machines of the session's bound set at that vendor stopped until the operator replaces it". Whether a harness-composed job (`digest_secret`, `delivery_reboot`, `replace_root_label`) is refused under the hold is unsettled, and ADR-0050 stops every box-plane job "whoever starts it" for a machine's destructive disposition.

ADR-0038 records: "Abandonment still has no typed destroy to run at such a vendor, and `ARC-21` and `ARC-22` now hand the act to the operator; while a disposition naming abandonment or a destructive reinstall stands on the scope, `STA-24` holds every further call under it and the model's box-plane commands to the set's machines at that vendor until the operator replaces the disposition (ADR-0044)."
close_reason: Specified that under an untyped vendor scope a destructive disposition's hold refuses every new box-plane job to a machine it covers, whoever starts it (STA-24), with coverage anchored on the approving session's bound set and its lawful growth up to its final recorded reach. The destructive hold carries by exact origin to a later untyped scope's calls only, and an unresolved call is inherited at the same exact origin under a changed credential; neither carries by vendor identity across origins. SEC-4 closes local permission when its session ends, and resupplying the credential or accepting the mode alone carries no permission over. A successor keeps the pause on the same covered machine under the same credential; the pause's other succession edges stay open in T47. CNF-105 gains the discriminating cases, a destructive replacement stays a hold, and ARC-15, SEC-14, STA-23, T47 and ADR-0038/0044/0050 point to the owners. ADR-0054 records it. Specified, not enabled; runtime remains outstanding.

comments.text:
## Owner decision — destructive untyped-scope hold, 2026-11-02

Selected A: the destructive hold on an untyped vendor scope stops every new box-plane machine job within its existing covered vendor and bound-set reach, whoever starts it. This includes model commands and harness-started work such as a digest, reboot, delivery-check read, relabel or key-migration job. Record this as an amendment, not as a claim that the former model-only wording already supplied an unambiguous general rule.

Existing-record collection and the local paste remain available under their existing independent guards. A freshly issued read job is a new command, not collection of an existing record. A local paste sends nothing to the machine and neither clears the hold nor authorizes a job. This choice overrides no separate machine deletion, pin, binding, command-hold, custody or other admission requirement.

Keep the current scope/vendor/set boundary and the existing operator replacement of a destructive disposition as the way to release this hold. The operator's action by hand at the vendor does not release it by itself. No new inheritance or clearance rule is selected for token rotation, re-approved scopes or session succession; those T47 questions remain queued. This amendment creates no new recovery sweep or protection for journal-omitted work.

Put the new scope-hold duty in STA-24, and coordinate CNF-105, the T47 record and affected ADR-0038/0050 references after the rule is amended. Retain permitted collection and local paste, and show an otherwise eligible job admitted after a continuing replacement. A deliberately admitted harness job while the destructive scope hold stands must produce the targeted CNF-105 refusal-control finding. Keep other vendors and machines outside the hold's defined reach unaffected.

This choice is settled. No rule implementation, runtime evidence or stage-2 admission is claimed by this record. The token-rotation/scope-succession questions and the other vendor/recovery beads remain separate.

## Source quotations — current text to preserve or amend

These are quotations of the current source, not claims that the selected amendments have already landed. The selected changes and the queued limits remain as recorded above.

`STA-24` (03-state-and-recovery.md:559):

> A destructive disposition on a scope refuses every further call under the scope
> and keeps the model's box-plane commands to the machines of the session's bound set at that
> vendor stopped until the operator replaces it. Before either destructive choice the screen
> MUST say that the harness cannot carry it out there and that the operator acts at the vendor by
> hand; doing so releases nothing by itself, and the replacement does. Machines outside the bound
> set, or at another vendor, are not held by this (`SEC-4`, ADR-0038).

`STA-20` (03-state-and-recovery.md:130):

> Collecting a job record is not held, and other
> machines are unaffected. Collection MUST remain an available fresh privileged read of the
> existing record, including while ordinary commands and harness jobs are held. It MUST NOT
> require a new setup job or pass through ordinary `exec` admission.

`ARC-43` (01-architecture.md:486):

> The local paste writes
> nothing to the machine; no scan material goes to the page, machine or sheet.

comments.text:
## Technical settlement — untyped-scope rotation and succession boundaries, 2026-11-03

The independent readings agree on these source consequences and none calls these points a new amendment. This record selects no new inheritance policy, scope-permission lifetime or successor-session machine-hold rule. The prior owner-selected all-new-jobs A amendment remains recorded separately and pending normative implementation.

When an outstanding untyped call exists, reapproval with the same exact origin and credential inherits that call. A new approval or call identifier does not clear it. The new untyped call is refused, including one described as a read. In the stipulated properly admitted successor using that same credential, the inherited unresolved call still refuses a new call and retains its pause on the same covered machine. This is the existing same-credential rule, not a new restriction on every replacement credential after memory loss. The mechanism for recognizing credential equality after local erasure is not established by this record and supplies no permission to persist a new secret hash or token fingerprint.

A destructive disposition is terminal with the operation outcome still unknown, so it is not the outstanding call named by that inheritance sentence. The old disposition remains standing on its own resource. Calls under that original scope remain refused. A new approval of that same resource cannot replace its disposition merely by receiving a new identifier; admitting a genuinely distinct successor scope is the unresolved policy case rather than an automatically established resource identity.

While the original session still lives and the machine remains within the original vendor and bound-set reach, reapproval or a replacement token for another scope does not release the old hold on new machine jobs. Model commands remain held by the current source; harness-started digest, reboot, relabel and other new jobs are held by the already selected pgp A amendment. No new requester ballot is needed. This technical agreement is limited to the original live-session case; successor-session applicability is not selected by it.

Each actual new acting session needs its own eligible binding and named-mode acceptance before its untyped call. Neither historical acceptance nor retained credentials revive ended runtime authority. An ordinary surviving hide differs from actual end. The separate owner-selected lifetime A in the section “Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03” on this bead requires fresh successor scope approval; if the current card expressly both approves the scope and accepts the mode, one act can do both and no extra click is selected.

Known-machine exclusivity is checked independently, against origin or vendor identity and retained journal facts. A new token or an unsupported claim of a different account does not evade that check. A subset example that excludes an undestroyed known machine at the relevant origin/vendor identity is already refused and is not evidence for a useful new inheritance policy. Existing box-plane reach remains limited to its covered vendor and bound-set machines; no new hold on unrelated vendors or machines is selected.

Existing-record collection and local paste remain available under independent authority, pins, scan and custody guards. A new machine read job is a new command, not record collection. No untyped vendor call becomes a typed reconciliation read merely by its name.

Manual work or its report, late observations, key replacement, local buffer clearing and actual session end are not themselves the operator's replacement of the standing disposition. A true service revocation ends that credential's external authority under its existing disposal rule, but proves no machine deletion or operation success and does not replace the disposition. No new generic revocation oracle or manual-work confirmation protocol is adopted. Externally live credential exposure retains its existing trust-display lifetime, independently of local permission and runtime memory.

## Source quotations

STA-24 says "A scope re-approved for the same origin and credential inherits the outstanding call."

STA-24 says "nothing under a scope counts as a read, because nothing types it."

STA-24 says "a disposed call is not an open one."

STA-24 says "doing so releases nothing by itself, and the replacement does."

STA-20 says "Collection MUST remain an available fresh privileged read of the existing record, including while ordinary commands and harness jobs are held."

STA-23 says "Individual session end destroys that session's runtime authority and pending approvals; it does not revive on return."

SEC-14 says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it."

SEC-4 says "The scope MUST be refused if any undestroyed machine provisioned through that origin, or through that vendor identity, lies outside the calling session's bound set; and while the scope stands, no such machine is bound to another session."

STA-24 says "Machines outside the bound set, or at another vendor, are not held by this".

The owner separately selected exact-origin destructive-call inheritance B, recorded in the section “Owner decision — destructive-hold inheritance for later scope calls, 2026-11-03” on this bead; this technical-common record does not itself select that amendment. The owner separately selected changed-token unresolved-call inheritance A in the section “Owner decision — unresolved-call inheritance after a credential change, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The owner separately selected local permission lifetime A in the section “Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The owner separately selected successor-job applicability A in the section “Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03” on this bead, retaining its disputed classification. The scope/session-succession frontier is closed. Manual vendor-work recording and non-vendor scopes remain separately queued. The selected unresolved-call A supplies the post-erasure later-scope call result without selecting a credential-recognition mechanism or the disputed historical forced-refusal derivation. No current Dispatch theorem carries the untyped pause/hold, and no route is admitted by this source reconciliation.

No normative edit, tracker transition, readiness or closure is claimed.

## Owner decision — destructive-hold inheritance for later scope calls, 2026-11-03

Selected B as an amendment: a standing destructive hold on an untyped vendor scope carries to every later scope at the same exact origin after token rotation or reapproval. Calls through that later scope remain refused while the inherited destructive hold stands, regardless of credential equality, approval identifier or overlap with the original held machines. A fresh eligible session does not bypass this call restriction by approving a later scope at the same origin. Inheritance supplies no approval or binding authority of its own.

The original valid disposition and the calls it disposed retain their identities and resource. No journal rewriting or synthetic settlement is selected. The existing operator replacement of that disposition remains the release route under STA-24. A new token, approval, manual vendor action/report or local Lock is not itself that replacement. Exact-origin inheritance is not vendor-identity inheritance across other origins.

The origin-wide option was one reading's actual pick and simplest option. Its strongest argument was that once the credential is erased, equality with a pasted key cannot be established, making origin the simpler available boundary. That argument is recorded as the reader's rationale, not as a unanimous proof that every possible credential-recognition mechanism is impossible or that all changed-token unresolved calls were already refused.

The other two readings chose A, original origin plus overlap with the originally held machines. One called A the simplest protective option. The other called C, treating genuinely new scopes separately, mechanically simplest while explicitly not recommending it. Neither A nor C was selected. The remaining distinct unchosen proposals were D, same-credential-only carry; E, an explicit operator predecessor link; F, verified-account proof lineage; G, refuse the new scope approval itself; and H, vendor-identity carry across origins. No profile/account-proof protocol or additional approval refusal is silently included in B.

This decision covers destructive-hold inheritance for calls only. The earlier all-new-machine-jobs hold A remains unchanged. In the same live session, jobs already within the original vendor/bound-set hold remain held after token changes; that result was already settled and was not another ballot. The owner separately selected unresolved-call inheritance A in the section “Owner decision — unresolved-call inheritance after a credential change, 2026-11-03” on this bead after a focused panel. The owner separately selected local permission lifetime A in the section “Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The owner separately selected successor-job applicability A in the section “Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The scope/session-succession frontier is closed. Do not adopt the broader unresolved-call portion of the origin-wide reader proposal or its source interpretation of successor jobs through this calls-only answer.

## Source quotations and owning work

STA-24 says "A scope re-approved for the same origin and credential inherits the outstanding call."

STA-24 says "a disposed call is not an open one."

STA-24 says "doing so releases nothing by itself, and the replacement does."

SEC-14 says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it."

The first quoted inheritance sentence owns an outstanding call and is not a claim that the new destructive-call inheritance was already specified. Implement the selected call relationship at STA-24, with coordinated T47 and ADR-0038/0044 records and stage-2 conformance. Retain existing SEC-4 eligibility/exclusivity and SEC-14 acceptance, raw-secret custody, pending approvals, record collection/local paste and other admissions. No new token fingerprint, credential-derived durable reference, account proof or runtime framework is selected.

Distinguish refusal of calls through a later scope at the same origin after reapproval/rotation, including a scope not shown to overlap old machine reach, from otherwise eligible calls after the old disposition's valid replacement and at unrelated origins. Preserve the original source record and continuing-replacement semantics, failed append/replay behavior and the separately selected same-session all-new-jobs refusal. Do not infer a new cross-origin hold or use this call amendment to decide the queued successor machine-job policy. The current formal companion omits untyped pause/hold semantics; existing theorems supply no implementation or admission evidence for this change.

This is a decision record, not a normative edit or completion/readiness claim.

## Technical settlement — focused untyped-scope residual review, 2026-11-03

The independent readings agree on the following narrow source consequences and none calls these points a new amendment. This technical record does not itself select a new policy. The owner separately selected exact-origin unresolved-call inheritance A in the section “Owner decision — unresolved-call inheritance after a credential change, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The owner separately selected local permission lifetime A in the section “Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The owner separately selected successor-job applicability A in the section “Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03” on this bead; the pgp residual frontier is closed. Earlier all-new-jobs A and destructive-calls-only B remain separately selected decisions awaiting normative implementation.

Let O name the exact origin, K1 and K2 the credentials, and U the unresolved call. In a surviving live session with U under O/K1 and a distinguishably different K2 still recognizable in memory, current same-origin-and-credential inheritance does not attach that call to a scope approved for O/K2 merely because the origin matches. An otherwise eligible new K2 call can proceed subject to all other guards. This is the stated current boundary, not selection of it as the future policy. Extending unresolved-call inheritance to all later scopes at O is the separately owner-selected A amendment; this paragraph records its pre-amendment baseline only. The original U stays recorded and unresolved, and the original live-session machine pause remains. The chosen destructive-call B does not apply to this example because it contains no destructive disposition.

Same-origin same-credential outstanding-call inheritance remains mandatory. Another approval identifier, call identifier or actual session end does not erase the required result. Memory erasure supplies no permission to violate that obligation, and no new durable secret fingerprint, value-derived reference or account-proof protocol is selected by identifying a recognition gap. The readings disagree that every later credential was already blocked at O after erasure under the former same-credential text. The separate owner-selected A now supplies the same-origin later-scope call result without credential comparison; it does not settle that historical derivation as consensus.

Actual session end differs from a surviving ordinary hide. Ended runtime authority cannot revive; a successor needs eligible binding and its own applicable named-mode acceptance. If a current card explicitly approves scope use and accepts the mode, one action may do both. No second click is required by this technical agreement. The separately selected lifetime A now requires fresh successor approval; the panel classification disagreement is retained in that decision record.

The source distinguishes local permission closure from external bearer-key validity and disclosure. A historical record or live exposure display is neither a new scope approval nor evidence of service revocation. Scope exclusivity must be checked before alleging a useful successor binding. No machine-job policy is selected by stipulating an otherwise eligible successor.

The original live session's lawful set growth must not be lost by freezing a hold at the instant its disposition was recorded. Likewise, a successor's other machines do not automatically become part of the earlier session's original reach. These reach boundaries are preserved without choosing whether or how the original hold applies to a genuinely new successor's machine jobs. All readers favor preserving the hold on the original machine, but one calls that carry an amendment, so it was not self-settled. The owner subsequently selected A in the section “Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03” on this bead.

## Source quotations

STA-24 says "A scope re-approved for the same origin and credential inherits the outstanding call."

ADR-0038 says "a token rotated at the same origin starts with no unresolved barrier".

STA-24 says "a disposed call is not an open one."

STA-23 says "Individual session end destroys that session's runtime authority and pending approvals; it does not revive on return."

SEC-14 says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it."

SEC-1 says "A set grows by one operator act per machine, and never shrinks while its session lives."

ADR-0017 says "closing the approval stops new calls, but it does not invalidate a bearer key the service has seen".

The current live-session changed-key admission and the proposed tighter rule must not be conflated. The owner selected the new unresolved-call boundary A as an amendment, recorded separately; a common preferred outcome did not turn it into a clarification. Local permission lifetime A is separately owner-selected; successor-job applicability A is also separately owner-selected, with its classification disagreement retained. Manual-work records, non-vendor scopes, account identity, any recognition mechanism needed for a separate purpose, old-machine deletion reconciliation and ordinary half-finished binding after Lock remain separate.

This is a technical record, not a normative edit, implementation evidence, readiness or closure.

## Owner decision — unresolved-call inheritance after a credential change, 2026-11-03

Selected A as an amendment: after a credential change, every later untyped vendor scope at the same exact origin inherits the unresolved call. Credential inequality does not exempt that later scope from the inherited unresolved-call barrier. Inheritance supplies no approval or binding authority; all other admissions still apply.

The accepted cost is that a genuinely different account at the same origin is also blocked until the original call has a valid terminal record. This is exact-origin inheritance, not vendor-identity inheritance across different origins. The original call and scope retain their identities and recorded uncertainty. No automatic retry, resource rewrite or synthetic settlement is selected.

All three independent readings picked A and called the live changed-credential extension an amendment. The first called A simplest; its strongest argument was that different tokens can reach the same account. The second called A the simplest conservative option; its strongest argument was that different credential bytes establish no separation for an untyped operation. The third recommended A because a fresh token recreates the fresh-identifier bypass, but called keeping the same-credential boundary B simplest together with its own disputed post-erasure reading. Do not report unanimous agreement about simplicity or retroactively call the selected amendment existing behavior.

Unchosen alternatives were B, retain the same-credential boundary; C, permit the different-credential call while showing the outstanding call on its scope card; D, explicit operator linkage between scopes; E, refuse the new scope approval itself while the call remains unresolved; and F, inheritance only where the new scope overlaps the original machine reach. No warning-only exception, operator linkage, account-proof mechanism or new approval refusal is included in A. Attribution is not reproduced here.

The selected exact-origin rule also determines the call result after local credential erasure: while the original call remains unresolved, a later scope at that origin inherits it without needing credential comparison. This is a consequence of the owner's amendment. It does not establish the disputed claim that universal post-erasure refusal was already forced by the former same-credential text, nor prove that every possible recognition method was impossible. No separate refusal of scope approval, blanket refusal after valid terminal reconciliation, or new persistent secret fingerprint is selected.

Destructive-hold inheritance B remains unchanged and separate. A valid terminal record ends the unresolved-call barrier under its existing rules; a destructive disposition then engages B, while a continuing disposition does not create a destructive hold. Actual session end, credential erasure, reapproval and manual vendor activity are not themselves terminal reconciliation. The original live-session machine pause remains under its existing reach. The owner separately selected local permission lifetime A in the section “Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03” on this bead. The owner separately selected successor-job applicability A in the section “Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03” on this bead; this call-inheritance answer itself decided neither.

## Source quotations and owning work

STA-24 says "A scope re-approved for the same origin and credential inherits the outstanding call."

ADR-0038 says "a token rotated at the same origin starts with no unresolved barrier".

STA-24 says "a disposed call is not an open one."

SEC-14 says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it."

Those first two quotations describe the existing boundary being amended, not the selected rule already implemented. The normative inheritance owner is STA-24; coordinate T47 and ADR-0038 and retain stage-2 conformance cases for changed credentials and post-erasure succession, with unrelated-origin and valid-terminal positive boundaries. No new raw-secret custody, account-recognition protocol or capability enablement is selected. Existing formal results do not establish this untyped inheritance policy.

This is a decision record, not a normative edit, readiness or closure claim.

## Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03

Selected A: when a session actually ends, its local untyped vendor-scope permission and exclusivity close. A successor approves afresh, on the same card where it accepts the mode. The one card act may expressly approve and accept together; no additional confirmation step is selected. Resupplying a credential or accepting the mode alone does not carry the ended session's permission into the successor.

All three independent readings picked A and called it simplest. Two called it an amendment resolving the reserved lifetime policy; the third called it a source-forced clarification. Record the explicit owner resolution with that classification disagreement intact. Agreement about the preferred behavior was not permission to self-settle a disputed amendment.

The strongest arguments were a clear authority boundary without orphaned exclusivity; current-session approval with exposure history retained; and the risk that persistent exclusivity otherwise blocks successor entry. The last argument favored A but did not establish that every explicit-close or transfer alternative was impossible.

The alternatives not selected were B, reuse historical permission after the successor's fresh mode acceptance, including automatic transfer; C, keep local permission and exclusivity until explicit local closure, then approve anew; and D, explicit successor adoption of the historical permission. An adoption that itself authorizes successor calls is substantively a fresh local approval. Also considered and rejected were E, permission remaining attached to the ended session; F, timer expiry; and G, expiry on ordinary hide. Ordinary hide remains distinct from actual end. Attribution is not reproduced here.

Local permission closure does not establish external credential revocation, erase history or end disclosure of a still-exposed credential. Retained calls and standing dispositions keep their records. The separately selected unresolved-call inheritance A and destructive-call inheritance B are unchanged; fresh approval does not evade either. No new raw-secret custody, account-proof mechanism or permission transfer protocol is selected.

Closing the old local exclusivity removes that particular obstacle to successor binding. It does not grant binding authority or waive current origin/vendor-identity, known-machine, independence, capability or other admissions. The owner separately selected successor-job applicability A in the section “Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03” on this bead. Closing local permission did not itself decide that machine-job policy.

## Source quotations and owning work

STA-23 says "Individual session end destroys that session's runtime authority and pending approvals; it does not revive on return."

SEC-4 says "The scope MUST be refused if any undestroyed machine provisioned through that origin, or through that vendor identity, lies outside the calling session's bound set; and while the scope stands, no such machine is bound to another session."

ARC-15 says "No untyped call runs before its scope is approved."

SEC-14 says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it."

ADR-0017 says "closing the approval stops new calls, but it does not invalidate a bearer key the service has seen".

Specify the selected local permission/exclusivity lifetime at SEC-4, coordinating ARC-15, SEC-14, STA-23 and the T47 reservation without duplicating the rule. Retain stage-2 conformance for actual end, lawful successor approval/acceptance, ordinary hide, continuing external exposure and inherited call restrictions. Existing formal results are not evidence that this untyped-scope lifetime policy is implemented.

This is a decision record, not a normative edit, readiness or closure claim.

## Owner decision — successor-job applicability of the destructive hold, 2026-11-03

Selected A: a successor's new jobs stay held on the originally covered machines until the operator replaces the destructive disposition. This covers the original set's lawful later growth up to its final recorded reach, but does not cover the successor's unrelated machines. The hold applies to every new box-plane job within that reach, whoever starts it, preserving the earlier all-new-jobs decision.

All three independent readings picked A and called it simplest. Two called successor applicability a clarification; the third called it an amendment requiring an explicit successor-job admission rule. Record the owner resolution with that disagreement intact. The strongest arguments were that the specified release had never occurred; that a session end must not bypass the standing destructive choice; and that Lock followed by re-entry must not stand in for the chosen wipe.

Unchosen alternatives were B, end job applicability with the old session; C, freeze coverage at the time the disposition was recorded; D, hold the successor's whole set at that vendor; E, carry the hold only if the successor also approves another vendor scope; and F, refuse successor binding until replacement. All readings rejected B as a bypass, although one called it mechanically short. C loses lawful later original-set growth; D broadens coverage to unrelated machines; E permits a successor without a new vendor scope to evade the job hold; F adds a binding refusal. Attribution is not reproduced here. None is selected by A.

The old disposition and scope retain their identity and history. A successor need not approve a new vendor scope for the original machine-job restriction to apply. Closing the predecessor's local scope permission/exclusivity under the separately selected lifetime A is not replacement of its destructive disposition. The unresolved-call A and destructive-call B decisions remain unchanged. Binding, capability and other admissions remain independent; this decision grants no new successor authority.

Existing-record collection and local paste retain their separate guards. A newly dispatched read, digest or reboot is a new job rather than collection of an existing record. Replacing the disposition releases this restriction subject to all other admissions; no automatic retry, operation-success inference or retrospective settlement is selected.

This closes the remaining scope/session-succession decisions for tw-pgp. It does not implement the amendments or establish runtime conformance. The disputed historical post-erasure proof remains unendorsed; the selected exact-origin call rule supplies the call result without that proof.

## Source quotations and owning work

STA-24 says "a disposed call is not an open one."

STA-24 says "doing so releases nothing by itself, and the replacement does."

STA-24 says "Machines outside the bound set, or at another vendor, are not held by this".

SEC-1 says "A set grows by one operator act per machine, and never shrinks while its session lives."

STA-20 says "Collection MUST remain an available fresh privileged read of the existing record, including while ordinary commands and harness jobs are held."

Specify successor-job applicability at STA-24, keeping original reach and the existing replacement release, coordinated with the other selected tw-pgp decisions and ADR-0044/0050. Retain stage-2 refusal coverage for successor model and harness jobs, including a successor without a later vendor scope, lawful original-set growth, and positive boundaries for unrelated machines, existing-record collection and valid disposition replacement. Existing formal results do not prove this untyped job-hold policy.

This is a decision record, not a normative edit or a closure/readiness claim for implementation.

- "Owner decision — destructive untyped-scope hold, 2026-11-02" (all-new-jobs A), comment 35000001.
- "Technical settlement — untyped-scope rotation and succession boundaries, 2026-11-03", comment 46000001.

- "Owner decision — local scope permission at actual session end, 2026-11-03" (A).

The records read "actual session end" against the session rules of 2026-11-03. tw-l1l's "Owner decision — sessions survive every local event until End, 2026-11-04" (comment 69000001) has since changed which events end a session: no local event does, and an explicit Lock is not one. Read "actual session end" as whatever ends a session under tw-l1l's landed text. A Lock, reload or ordinary hide is not one.

**Current gap.** `STA-24`'s hold "keeps the model's box-plane commands to the machines of the session's bound set at that vendor stopped until the operator replaces it". It names model commands only, so a harness-started job is unsettled. `STA-24`'s inheritance covers only "A scope re-approved for the same origin and credential", and ADR-0038 says "a token rotated at the same origin starts with no unresolved barrier". No text says when the local scope permission closes, or whether the hold reaches a successor's jobs. No current Dispatch theorem carries the untyped pause or hold.

**Desired behavior and owners:**

- **All new jobs are held** (35000001), at `STA-24`, recorded as an amendment, not as what the model-only wording already meant. While the destructive disposition stands, every new box-plane job within the covered vendor and bound-set reach is held, whoever starts it. That includes model commands, digest, reboot, delivery-check read, relabel and key-migration jobs. A freshly issued read job is a new command. Collection of an existing record stays available (`STA-20`: "Collection MUST remain an available fresh privileged read of the existing record, including while ordinary commands and harness jobs are held."), and so does the local paste, which sends nothing to the machine and neither clears the hold nor authorizes a job. The release stays the operator's replacement of the disposition: "doing so releases nothing by itself, and the replacement does." The new hold overrides no deletion, pin, binding, command-hold or custody requirement, and it creates no new recovery sweep or protection for journal-omitted work. None of these is the replacement: manual vendor work or its report, late observations, key replacement, a new token or approval, local buffer clearing, a Lock, or actual session end. A true service revocation ends that credential's external authority but proves no deletion or operation success, and it is not the replacement either.
- **Destructive-call inheritance** (B), at `STA-24`. A standing destructive hold carries to every later scope at the same exact origin after token rotation or reapproval. Calls through that later scope are refused, regardless of credential equality, approval id or overlap with the held machines. A fresh eligible session does not bypass it by approving a later scope at that origin. This is exact-origin inheritance, not vendor-identity inheritance across origins. Inheritance supplies no approval or binding authority. The original disposition and its calls keep their identities and resource, with no journal rewrite or synthetic settlement.
- **Unresolved-call inheritance** (A), at `STA-24`, amending its sentence "A scope re-approved for the same origin and credential inherits the outstanding call". Update ADR-0038's "a token rotated at the same origin starts with no unresolved barrier" to match. After a credential change, every later untyped scope at the same exact origin inherits the unresolved call, with no credential comparison. Accepted cost: a different account at the same origin is blocked until the original call has a valid terminal record. Same-origin, same-credential inheritance stays mandatory. Session end, credential erasure, reapproval and manual vendor work are not terminal reconciliation. A valid terminal record ends the barrier. A destructive disposition then engages B, and a continuing one creates no hold.
- **Local permission lifetime** (A), at `SEC-4`, coordinated with `ARC-15`, `SEC-14`, `STA-23` and the T47 record without duplicating the rule. At actual session end the local scope permission and its exclusivity close. The successor approves afresh, on the card where it accepts the mode, and one card act may both approve and accept. Resupplying a credential or accepting the mode alone carries no permission over. Closing permission is not external revocation, erases no history and ends no disclosure of a still-exposed credential.
- **Successor-job applicability** (A), at `STA-24`, coordinated with ADR-0044 and ADR-0050. A successor's new jobs stay held on the originally covered machines until the replacement, including the original set's lawful later growth up to its final recorded reach. The successor's unrelated machines are not held. The successor needs no new vendor scope for the hold to apply. Closing the predecessor's local permission is not the replacement.
- **Settled boundaries** (46000001 and the residual review): no token fingerprint, credential-derived durable reference, account proof or runtime framework. Known-machine exclusivity is checked independently, and a new token does not evade it. No untyped call becomes a typed read by its name. Machines outside the bound set, or at another vendor, stay unaffected.
- **Records to coordinate after the rules change:** `CNF-105`, the T47 record, and ADR-0038, ADR-0044 and ADR-0050's references.

**Stop and report — choose none of these:**

- Manual vendor-work recording and non-vendor scopes. Both stay queued separately.
- Any credential-recognition mechanism, and the disputed historical claim that the former same-credential text already forced refusal after erasure. The selected exact-origin rule gives the call result without it.
- Proposals not selected:
  - for the calls (B): A, origin plus overlap; C, new scopes separate; D, same-credential only; E, an operator predecessor link; F, verified-account lineage; G, refusing the new scope approval; H, vendor-identity carry across origins;
  - for unresolved calls (A): B, keep the same-credential boundary; C, allow the call and show the outstanding one; D, operator linkage; E, refusing the new approval; F, overlap only;
  - for permission lifetime (A): B, reuse after fresh acceptance or automatic transfer; C, keep until explicit close; D, explicit adoption; E, attached to the ended session; F, a timer; G, expiry on hide;
  - for successor jobs (A): B, ending with the old session; C, freezing coverage at the disposition; D, the successor's whole set at that vendor; E, only with another vendor scope; F, refusing successor binding.
- Any edit that would weaken a theorem, gate, assumption boundary or requirement beyond what a named decision qualifies, or enable an untyped scope. Stop and report the conflict.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Each duty has one normative home, and the other places point to it. Every sentence asserting what another requirement says carries its quote, and the citation gate passes. Where a touched clause is formalized, change its Lean declaration and its prose together. Existing theorems supply no evidence for these untyped rules; do not cite them as such.
- The amendments land with their ADR context: one new ADR, or amendment notes on ADR-0038, ADR-0044 and ADR-0050, recording each decision and the readings not selected.
- Conformance cases, as items of the "Untyped scopes, the jump host, sets above one" row:
  - a deliberately admitted harness job under a standing destructive hold produces the targeted `CNF-105` refusal-control finding;
  - existing-record collection and the local paste stay available under the hold, and a fresh read job is refused;
  - an otherwise eligible job is admitted after a continuing replacement;
  - calls through a later scope at the same origin are refused after rotation or reapproval, including a scope with no overlap shown; calls after a valid replacement, and at an unrelated origin, are admitted;
  - a changed credential at the same origin inherits the unresolved call; after local credential erasure, a later scope at the same origin inherits it with no credential comparison; a valid terminal record ends the barrier; an unrelated origin is unaffected;
  - at actual session end the permission and exclusivity close; a successor approves and accepts in one card act; a Lock, reload or hide closes nothing; closing the permission ends no exposure display of a still-exposed credential; a successor's fresh approval evades neither inheritance rule;
  - a successor's model and harness jobs stay held on the original machines, including one with no later vendor scope and one on lawful original-set growth; the successor's unrelated machines are admitted; the successor's existing-record collection and its jobs after a valid replacement are admitted;

**Out of scope:** enabling an untyped scope or any other capability; manual vendor-work recording; non-vendor scopes; account identity; runtime code; tw-l1l's own decisions.

This brief makes no normative edit and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Does a destroyed machine free the other machines' held output?

`CNF-95(f)` says "With neither, one or both pasted, output on A and B is released only after both."

ADR-0050 rejected "Release the other machines' output without the disposed machine's references" because "`SEC-5` says "Unscanned bytes MUST be withheld"; a secret copied onto another machine would go unscanned."

No text says whether M's confirmed destruction (at LNVPS, the vendor's confirmed deletion) releases A and B's withheld output, or whether their later output is still scanned for M's secret.

Bound sets of more than one machine are stage 2 (`STG-22`).

## Owner decision — deletion, retired references and held output, 2026-11-02

Selected A: confirmed deletion of M ends M's placed-secret scan reference and M's unarmed-reference wait. Bytes withheld before that deletion remain withheld: deletion never counts as a scan. Output produced after deletion is no longer checked for M's value, and the display states that limit. No peer-reference lifetime extension or release of the old withheld backlog is selected.

SEC-5 states: "Exact copies of a placed secret whose reference the browser holds are redacted from box-plane output before that output reaches the model or the transcript, and the claim is no wider than that." Its coverage limit is "It covers only placements whose reference the browser holds". Row 23 removes the persistent comparison material on destruction. Preserve those boundaries and "Unscanned bytes MUST be withheld": no old range becomes scanned, safe or releasable because a reference retired. Fresh output still owes every other applicable scan and release prerequisite.

Use stable record or range identity to retain the old withholding decision across later collection. The same pre-deletion job output range cannot pass as new output because it is re-collected, replayed, re-requested, displayed after deletion or assigned a later retrieval time. A range whose eligibility as post-deletion production is not established cannot be promoted to new output merely because its collection is late. This calls for protected non-secret identity and classification, not retention or export of raw application values, bare digests or expired scan material.

Retiring M's unarmed-reference wait lifts only that reference prerequisite. It clears no command hold, resource barrier, pending check, other unarmed-reference requirement, destructive restriction or unknown command outcome; it does not shrink an actual session's membership or authorize new contact with a deleted machine. A stop, renewal-off, deletion date, reinstall or disposition is not this deletion boundary. Use the admitted durably recorded deletion confirmation, with its existing evidence limits, rather than claiming irreversible physical erasure or revocation of the credential at its service.

The normative amendment belongs in SEC-5's scan/lifetime transition and ARC-43's required-reference/release rule, with SEC-6's coverage display and CNF-95(e/f) coordinated after the rules change. Add a targeted control that releases a pre-deletion unscanned backlog after deletion and require the CNF-95 finding. Include recollection of that same old range as a refusal and useful fresh-output admission after the selected boundary, subject to the remaining active references. Preserve cross-chunk matching for all references still required.

Peer-output effects are stage 2; this decision admits no larger set or new capability and supplies no runtime evidence. It changes neither service revocation policy nor tw-i55's human part. the confirmation, and refuse release, not the collection read (STA-20). The neither-pasted
branch adds the display, later-retrieval and machine-claimed-time refusals, a window spanning
withheld and fresh output, and exported-sheet custody. A pasted-before-destruction branch shows
the reference leaving persistence, and the LNVPS path exercises retirement on M alone. The
ADR-0050 amendment, dated at landing, and the atlas bullet quote their sources.

Gate exits before the change (main at a9ca43b, unpiped): check-all 0, unit suite 0. The mutation
controls on that tree were still running at close. The citation and atlas checks pass on this
tip. The full local gates on this branch's tip run as a user unit alongside the merge, and their
exits are recorded on the pull request.

Left open, not chosen here, for the owner:
- Scope of "bytes withheld before it stay withheld": whether it covers a range held only for
  another machine's unarmed reference and already scanned against the destroyed machine's
  references, once that other reference is re-armed.
- Whether a new command that reads a pre-destruction output file on a peer is new output, or a
  re-request of the old range.

title: Reduce UX friction: adopt the 2026-11-07 review's disposition
description:
Adopt the owner-accepted recommendations from the review "tau-web-spec: Recommendations to reduce
UX friction" (2026-11-07), which reviewed revision 4d991cde33ed07095815b3b33b6fa6b89f082db9. The
review's labels R01–R12 belong to that document and are not requirement identifiers; each child
bead carries the recommendation text it needs, so the review need not be reopened.

## Disposition (the review's own section 7, adopted as the default scope)

- **Interface direction now (spec wording only):** R09 installation preview, R10 backup checklist,
  R11 separated recovery progress, R12 resumable external handoffs, existing setup-approval
  batching (with R07's already-permitted batching), one inference Start surface (R08 A and D) and
  concise mode restatement under the existing SEC-14 policy (R05, first half). In this
  specification-only repository this means clarifying normative or explanatory wording in each
  rule's owning clause. No UI specification is invented.
- **Narrow contract amendments, owner-directed:** R01 Restore-verification retry, R02 conservative
  ad-hoc class by default (reverses part of ADR-0034), R03 explicit personal-goal reuse (reverses
  part of ADR-0034), R04 prospective correction of a mistaken revocation report (reverses part of
  ADR-0062; needs a versioned report-correction format), R06 cancellation-scoped deletion
  verification (reverses part of ADR-0053), and R08's locale-decimal input (owner pick 2026-11-08,
  "Accept the comma"). R01, R02, R03, R06 and R08's locale-decimal input relax current requirements
  on the owner's instruction; R04 tightens future protection but widens SEC-5 and ARC-43 as
  written. Each commit, PR and ADR names its relaxation or widening.
- **Revisit with targeted evidence (filed, not drafted):** R05's relevance-based omission, R07's
  provider-resolved destination authorization, R08's default paid-session duration and R08's
  real-issuer validation.

## Discipline for every child (review section 5)

1. Change the owning requirement; one rule, one home, pointers elsewhere.
2. Update directly dependent profile, format, conformance and formal text.
3. Record the policy decision in an ADR only where a deliberate decision is reversed.
4. Run the repository's existing required checks.

No workflow engine, risk scorer, generic undo framework or new schema layer. R04's versioned
correction encoding is the single named exception. Never enable a gated capability (R06 grants
permission only; T44's vendor-key capability stays unavailable). Never weaken a theorem, gate or
assumption boundary beyond what an amendment needs; anything further goes to the owner first. Every
claim about another requirement quotes it (AGENTS.md). The specification describes the system: no
stage gating or deferral by stage.

## Properties every child retains (review section 4)

Authenticated host identity; durable intent before effects; unknown outcomes stay unknown; explicit
financial and destructive authority; bound-set and credential isolation; independent delivery
checks; secret custody and output protection; same-session continuity. The review recommends no
per-command approvals, timer-based release of uncertain operations, unpinned fallback after a
mismatch, silent inference renewal or merging of distinct credentials.

title: Delivery declaration approval reads as an installation preview
description:
Review item R09 (interface improvement under the current contract; clarifying wording only).

## Current contract

ARC-39's delivery declaration is a structured statement of what must be true of the finished
machine. The model proposes typed values from the goal, starting from the signed ad-hoc minimum,
and the operator approves in plain language. Every field must be present; an unspecified field
prevents Delivered. The ad-hoc minimum is already complete and the ad-hoc access model is already
maintained, so ordinary setup needs no schema form and no access-model choice. Model-written checks
are reports, not authoritative delivery tests.

## Change

Add clarifying wording at the declaration's owning clause (ARC-39, with the delivery-declaration
design note only if it restates the approval surface) so a later reader does not over-build the
approval. The review's suggested clarification:

> The declaration schema is an internal contract, not a required user form. Ordinary approval
> presents its meaningful effects in plain language and may occur on the existing setup review. The
> exact accepted declaration must be recorded before installation.

The approval may read as an installation preview combining facts the declaration and existing setup
records already own: what will be installed, who can reach it (public listeners and access
restrictions), whether it keeps running (startup and restart), which application secrets it needs
and where they go, known costs, and how completion is judged. Departures from the signed minimum are
shown prominently; the structured form stays available in details. The preview combines
presentation only: it invents no field and moves no ownership.

## Boundaries

- Unspecified facts and failed authoritative checks never become success because the preview is
  simpler. The exact proposal recorded is the one summarized.
- Changes to exposed services or other approved facts are shown before acting on them.
- No separate proposal, schema-review, confirmation and final-confirmation screens; no new
  approval type. Check the existing setup batching rule (ARC-15) before saying where approval
  happens, and quote it.

## Acceptance

- The owning clause states the schema is internal and approval is a plain-language review that may
  be the existing setup review, with the exact accepted declaration recorded before installation.
- No requirement is weakened; any conformance item that names a user-facing declaration form is
  aligned or left unchanged with reason.
- check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Operator may explicitly reuse their own saved goal
description:
Review item R03: allow explicit reuse of the operator's own saved goals. Contract amendment on the
owner's instruction that reverses part of a deliberate decision. **Relaxation:** the blanket ban on
reusing a stored goal in another session is lifted for profiles that permit goals and declare no
independence bound. Name this relaxation in the commit, PR and ADR; record the reversal in a new ADR
that supersedes the relevant part of ADR-0034 (do not rewrite ADR-0034's history).

Owners to amend: ARC-11a, relevant profile wording, and the decision recorded in ADR-0034.

## Current contract

A goal is scoped to one session; the harness must not import, share or reuse it, including applying
a stored goal to another session. Goals are separately prohibited for profiles declaring an
independence bound. The built-in ad-hoc profile declares no such bound. The ban blocks repeating an
installation on a replacement server, starting a new session with the same outcome after the last
ended, and a personal list of recurring maintenance goals.

## Change

Permit the operator to explicitly select their own retained goal text from the same local store for
a new session when every target profile permits goals and declares no independence bound. Show the
selected text, its source and the new target before Start; journal the selection and its provenance
with the new session. Carry over the instruction only. Candidate text:

> Where the target profiles permit goals and declare no independence bound, the harness MAY let the
> operator explicitly reuse their own retained goal text from the same local store for a new
> session. The selected text and source MUST be shown before admission and recorded with the new
> session. Reuse transfers no approval, credential, binding, execution outcome or authority.

## Boundaries

- No automatic cross-session propagation, sharing between operators, or marketplace of unsigned
  templates.
- A target with an independence bound still refuses the goal. The new session's authority,
  binding, limits and approvals are established normally.
- Same-session interruption recovery stays separate: returning to an eligible interrupted session
  resumes it under its existing contract, never through this new-goal path.
- The text is visible and editable; edits are recorded. No claim that prior commands rerun or that
  earlier results apply to the new machine.

## Acceptance (focused checks)

- Selecting an earlier personal goal populates a new session without copying authority.
- A target with an independence bound still refuses the goal.
- The new session records the chosen text and source, including edits.
- A failed or ended earlier session cannot transfer approvals or cause automatic command replay.
- New ADR records the reversal and its tradeoff (common-mode risk for independence-bound profiles
  is untouched). check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Operator may correct a mistaken revocation report prospectively
description:
Review item R04: let the operator correct a mistaken revocation report prospectively. Contract
amendment on the owner's instruction that reverses part of a deliberate decision, with the one
named exception to "no new schema layer": a small, versioned report-correction encoding. It
tightens future protection for the placement (it restores a protective requirement), and it
**widens** two rules as written: SEC-5's "nothing re-creates them" and ARC-43's "a paste or digest
record arms nothing for it", because the paste and digest re-arm become available again on a
corrected placement. ADR-0062 rejected this option for exactly that reason. Name the widening in the
commit, PR and ADR. Record the reversal of ADR-0062's finality in a new ADR that supersedes that part
(do not rewrite ADR-0062's history).

Owners to amend: ARC-43, SEC-5, SEC-6, STA-16, the affected credential-format clause (the
version-7 sheet ADR-0062 names), conformance clauses including CNF-42 and CNF-95(h) (named in
ADR-0062's Consequences), and ADR-0062.

## Current contract

When a placement's required scan reference is unarmed, the operator can report that its credential
was revoked at the external service. The report ends that placement's required reference and moves
it into operator-reported history. The report is final; a later paste or digest cannot re-arm it.
After a mistaken report the operator can revoke the real key externally, rotate the placement when
allowed, or destroy the machine, but cannot correct the report. A mistaken report can remove future
scanning for a credential that remains valid.

## Change

Allow a forward, journaled correction for a placement not independently ended by rotation or
confirmed destruction. The correction keeps the original report and timestamp in history, makes the
placement's future protective requirement active again, starts it unarmed, withholds affected future
model work and output until the re-arm or ordinary rotation path satisfies it, and uses fresh scan
material (no resurrected retired scan key, no claim a machine-reported value is the original
secret). Reuse the existing digest and local-paste re-arm procedures with narrowly amended
applicability; keep their provenance and coverage limits visible. Candidate text:

> The operator MAY correct a revocation report for a placement not independently ended by rotation
> or confirmed destruction. The correction MUST preserve the original report and restore a future
> required reference, initially unarmed, before affected output can be released. It MUST NOT recall
> previously released output, release previously withheld output, erase history, or claim that an
> external service reversed a revocation.

A durable append is the effective boundary; an append failure leaves the previous state in force
and is reported. Publication paths consult the corrected state before releasing output. The display
identifies the interval during which the placement had no active scan requirement. No second
approval ceremony just because it tightens protection.

## Format constraint

The correction cannot be encoded by clearing the existing report field. Make the smallest explicit,
versioned change to the credential format that preserves both facts. Older data is never silently
interpreted as corrected. No generic undo framework.

## Acceptance (focused checks)

- Correcting the wrong placement restores its future requirement while preserving the original
  report.
- Output ready before correction but released afterward is checked against the current protection
  state.
- Correction does not revive a placement independently ended by rotation or confirmed destruction.
- Export, Restore and replay retain both report and correction; older data is not read as
  corrected.
- Previously withheld output stays withheld; previously released output is not described as
  recovered or erased.
- Formal declarations change with the Markdown where formalized; no theorem weakened (stop and
  report if one must be). check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Abandon or retire approval may authorize follow-up deletion checks
description:
Review item R06: let machine cancellation include follow-up deletion checks. Contract amendment on
the owner's instruction. **Relaxation:** an approval to abandon or retire named machines may also
authorize later deletion reads for those machines, instead of one operator-initiated check per read.
Name this relaxation in the commit, PR and ADR. It partly reverses ADR-0053's recorded decision
("One deletion check. One operator-started check, outside any session"): record that in a new ADR
superseding that part (do not rewrite ADR-0053's history). **Permission only:** the T44 vendor-key capability
stays unavailable, and the text must say verification is unavailable until that capability exists.

Owners to amend: SEC-4 (which says "It is one check, started by the operator from the screen that
shows the machine (`ARC-22`); nothing starts it automatically"), ARC-21 (it owns the Abandon
approval and its card, where the new disclosure goes), relevant ARC-22 and STA-17 wording, ADR-0053,
and affected conformance cases.

## Current contract

A deletion check is a narrow operation outside any session; it reads evidence for one eligible
stopped machine under that machine's recorded vendor key. The operator initiates each check; nothing
starts it automatically. The machine stays shown as existing and billed until the required deletion
evidence is durably recorded; a stopped state or passed deletion date is insufficient. The vendor-key
capability is unavailable pending T44.

## Change

Let the existing Abandon setup or Retire old machine approval also authorize subsequent deletion
verification for its named machines, disclosed as "status will be checked while the app is
available". Same recorded machine identity, key, route and evidence predicate. Here cancellation
means abandonment or retirement, not Stop task, End session, cancelling inference or closing the
browser. Candidate text:

> Approval to abandon or retire named machines MAY also authorize subsequent deletion verification
> for those machines. Once the existing eligibility conditions hold, the harness MAY perform the
> existing deletion reads while the app is available, including after reopening, without a separate
> approval for each check. This authority grants no mutation, new target, model execution or session
> authority. Obligations end only when the existing deletion predicate is satisfied and durably
> recorded.

Bounded checks on relevant availability or reopening; no always-on polling service and no new
mandatory consent modal. Previously recorded approvals without this scope stay manual until the
operator extends them through an existing status action.

## Boundaries

- The check never repeats stop, destroy, reinstall or renewal-off calls and never uses another
  machine's key. Authenticated reads are still vendor contact. Lock and unavailable credentials
  prevent dispatch.
- The deletion predicate (correctly identified account read, complete listing omitting the target,
  qualifying machine-specific 404) is unchanged; no single observation substitutes for it.
- Never enable the T44-gated capability; until it exists the interface shows verification as
  unavailable. If the amendment would need to touch the gate itself, stop and report.

## Acceptance (focused checks)

- An approved eligible cancellation can collect status without another tap.
- Reopening continues only the authorized reads for the same machine.
- Wrong keys, wrong targets, missing capabilities and missing credentials admit no read.
- Elapsed time, transport failure and partial evidence do not mark the machine deleted.
- A failed append of qualifying evidence leaves deletion, billing and exposure duties unresolved.
- check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Evidence first: action-relevant omission of standing-mode labels
description:
Review item R05, second half: action-relevant omission of standing-mode labels. Policy amendment
that needs targeted evidence first. Filed for evidence; do not draft until the evidence below exists
and the owner directs it.

## Proposal under consideration

Amend SEC-14's blanket restatement so the main approval surface prominently shows only modes that
change the current action's target, credential exposure or consequences, with the full standing and
historical record in the trust display. Candidate text from the review:

> An irreversible-action review MUST prominently restate standing modes that materially affect the
> action's target, credential exposure or consequences. Relevance MUST follow harness-owned rules,
> not model judgment. Where relevance is uncertain, the mode MUST be shown. The full standing and
> historical record remains available in the trust display. Initial acceptance and acceptance
> required for a newly approved act remain unchanged.

A small mapping within existing approval types; no model-based risk scorer or policy service.
Examples: a secret-placement card connects an unpinned installation with root-capable model access
to the secret; an add-machine card keeps the set's combined exposure; a typed invoice card stresses
recipient, amount and billing; an unrelated no-brief explanation may sit in details.

## Evidence needed before drafting

- The concise-restatement interface (sibling bead) in use, and observation of whether repeated
  labels still detach from the decision on representative flows.
- A concrete, harness-owned relevance mapping per existing approval type, with the uncertain case
  defaulting to disclosure, reviewed against ADR-0035's combined-exposure rationale.

## Boundaries if later adopted

Current-action risks stay visible without expanding details; uncertain relevance means disclosure;
a new unpinned reinstall still obtains fresh acceptance; a failed stronger check still halts.
Removing the no-brief category is a separate decision. Synchronize the secret-placement,
untyped-scope and conformance references.

title: Evidence first: paid-session default duration
description:
Review item R08, part B: measure before changing the paid-session default duration. Filed for
evidence; do not amend the default until the evidence exists and the owner directs it. Labelled
needs-info: it waits on observations from the implementation's test flow, and there is nothing to
do here until they exist (unlike the issuer bead, where only a human can gather vendor evidence).

## Question

Does the offered 15-minute lifetime (selectable 1 to 1440 whole minutes, subject to the pinned
issuer profile) cause avoidable restarts in representative end-to-end setups? The lifetime starts at
the fixed issuer-time origin; delay, hidden time and suspension consume it; expiry ends the session.

## Evidence needed

Observe representative end-to-end setups, including provider waits and app switching, and record
whether the chosen duration covers useful work. Observation in the current test flow is enough; no
analytics platform is a prerequisite.

## If the evidence supports a change

Amend the offered default or define a supported task-appropriate recommendation, shown explicitly.
Never silently extend an existing session; no renewal, top-up or second mint within a session.

title: Validate the production inference issuer against the contract
description:
Review item R08, part C: validate the real production issuer before expanding inference machinery.
Needs vendor evidence that only a human can gather; no vendor account, production machine or cluster
is touched from this repository. Labelled ready-for-human for that reason (the duration bead is
needs-info because it waits on test-flow observations instead).

## Question

The contract has only a synthetic fixture profile; production minting stays refused until a real
issuer profile and dated evidence are reviewed and pinned. The fixture does not prove real cap
enforcement, units, affordability or clock semantics. Does the intended production issuer support
the required cap, expiry, authenticated time and accounting semantics?

## Evidence needed

Dated evidence from the intended issuer for cap enforcement, expiry, authenticated issuer time and
accounting units, sufficient to pin a real issuer profile under the existing profile requirement.

## If the issuer does not match

Resolve the mismatch in the contract and integration. Do not build exception handling around the
fixture or present it as production support. Fixture-only builds acquire no production minting
authority.

description:

separator in the inference cap input. The review marked it optional ("if desired"). Owner pick,

amendment needs; anything that would goes to the owner first.

The value confirmed is exactly the value the worker authorizes; refused forms stay refused;
