title: Recovery items read as one backup checklist
description:
Review item R10 (interface improvement; explanatory wording only). Credential roles and seed
display rules are out of scope.

## Current contract

The local unlock passphrase, seed backup and recovery-file passphrase have separate roles. The seed
appears only in its dedicated ceremony; redisplay requires the local passphrase; hiding during the
ceremony clears the display and interrupts completion. The ceremony completes by re-entering all
twelve words or explicitly skipping that check; neither proves a successful backup (ADR-0047's
all-or-zero choice). Imported seeds get no invented new ceremony. Maintained-cloud setup completion
separately requires confirmation that the current recovery file was saved. The recovery file does
not contain the seed.

## Change

Add explanatory wording at the owning clauses (seed ceremony and recovery export in
03-state-and-recovery.md; the save confirmation stays where credential-format-v1 owns it) so the
recovery items read as one checklist with distinct purposes:

| Item to retain | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Seed backup | Re-derives recorded identities |
| Current encrypted recovery file | Carries the metadata and recovery records required alongside the seed |
| Recovery-file passphrase | Decrypts that file |

The local unlock passphrase is explained separately as the way into this device's encrypted store.
Before the seed is displayed, the operator is told that switching apps hides it and that showing it
again needs unlock. "Check all words" and "Skip check" are equally understandable actions. The
current-file saved confirmation stays in the export view, with no extra modal. The interface says
plainly that the seed alone is insufficient for this recovery path.

## Boundaries

- No "I wrote it down" checkbox, partial-word quiz or second skip confirmation (ADR-0047).
- Skip records the existing completion choice without implying a verified backup.
- App switching during the ceremony clears the seed and return does not redisplay it; ordinary
  hide outside the ceremony keeps its separate behavior.
- No combining the seed into the recovery file, merging passphrases or weakening seed clearing.
- Wording points at each item's owner; it does not restate the rules in a second normative copy.

## Acceptance

- The owning text presents the three retained items and the separate unlock passphrase with their
  purposes, the pre-display warning, and the seed-alone-insufficient statement, without changing
  any credential custody rule or ceremony outcome.
- check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Restore and Replace status separates usable recovery from pending cleanup
description:
Review item R11 (interface improvement using existing state and permissions; explanatory wording
only).

## Current contract

Restore reuses recorded identities without revoking the old phone's access. An imported seed cannot
allocate new identities, even when a backup claims to be current; new allocation requires Replace
with a fresh seed. Replace can stay incomplete while old access or resource cleanup is unresolved,
yet new machines, sessions and allocations may proceed while an old LNVPS machine awaits deletion
evidence, and a held machine does not stop other machines migrating. ADR-0053 already names the
status-fatigue problem of one persistent "incomplete" banner.

## Change

At the owning Restore/Replace clauses, add wording that the status shows separate progress facts
derived from existing records, as display projections and not new canonical lifecycle states:

| Progress area | Example status |
|---|---|
| Existing-machine access | Restored and available |
| New allocations | Ready under the fresh seed, or unavailable under an imported seed |
| Old access | Retirement pending for a named machine or relay pass |
| Old resources | Deletion unconfirmed, still shown as existing and billed |
| Recovery export | Current file saved, or a new export still required |

The overall Replace or revocation result stays incomplete while required obligations remain; at the
same time completed work shows as complete and otherwise eligible actions stay available. The
imported-seed allocation restriction is explained before import, not discovered afterwards.

## Boundaries

- A working new relay pass is not evidence the old pass was revoked; a saved new recovery file does
  not imply old keys or passes were retired; restored access is distinct from permission to
  allocate.
- Pending steps survive reopening; completed steps stay complete. Missing credentials or an
  unavailable deletion capability show as actionable limitations, not indefinite loading.
- No new lifecycle state, no non-revoking fresh-root operation, no removal of the stale-counter
  protection, no change to completion predicates.
- Quote the owners rather than restating them: STA-17 owns Restore and Replace (including partial
  progress), STA-22b owns the imported-seed allocation restriction.

## Acceptance

- The owning text says Restore/Replace status is presented as separate projections from existing
  records with the overall result still incomplete while obligations remain, and that the
  imported-seed restriction is explained before import.
- No completion, allocation or deletion rule changes. check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: LNVPS external handoffs are visible and resumable
description:
Review item R12 (interface improvement and sequencing of already-required prerequisites;
explanatory wording only).

## Current contract

The LNVPS path verifies email under each machine's vendor identity; the same operator email can
serve those separate accounts but verification is account-specific. The operator opens the vendor
link and the harness confirms the matching authenticated account state; it reads no mail and creates
no mailbox. The path also has one machine invoice paid from the operator's wallet, manual
out-of-band enrollment of a derived relay public key by the publisher, and inference already funded.
There is no automated relay purchase or reacquisition. The per-machine vendor identity remains under
the T44 capability gate.

## Change

Owners: ARC-22 owns the unfinished-setup screen ("An unfinished setup MUST own the first screen …
Resume-or-abandon *is* the opening screen"), so the resumable-view wording goes there. STG-21 owns
LNVPS email verification; any email-specific wording goes there. ARC-30 owns invoice payment and
STG-18 only lists what the LNVPS path does not test: cite them, do not write setup-view behavior
into them. One rule, one home, pointers elsewhere.

At ARC-22 (with STG-21 for the email step), add wording that setup presents one resumable view with
the next needed action and its observed status, reusing recorded facts while preserving per-machine
scope, for example:

| Step | Useful status |
|---|---|
| Email | Waiting for verification of this machine's account |
| Relay | Waiting for publisher enrollment of the public key |
| Machine payment | Awaiting payment or qualifying vendor confirmation |
| Installation | Ready, running, blocked or complete with the actual reason |
| Recovery | Current file still needs to be saved |

Prerequisites are checked as early as the existing protocol allows, especially before a billable
order; a dependency on someone else (publisher enrollment) is said before the operator commits. On
return from email or wallet, status reconciles through the already-authorized evidence path. An
expired email link gets the exact supported route and its limits.

## Boundaries

- Opening the email link does not mark verification complete without the matching authenticated
  status. No operator attestation where the contract requires vendor evidence.
- Returning from a wallet preserves the original order, invoice and uncertainty; no new order
  because an external app interrupted the browser.
- No promise of resend, automated enrollment or reacquisition. This path is one machine invoice,
  not a three-purchase wallet flow.
- The delivery screen distinguishes infrastructure delivery from whether Hermes and its provider
  are functionally working.
- The file name 06-first-stage.md is not a reason to gate or defer anything by stage. Never enable
  the T44-gated capability.

## Acceptance

- The owning text describes the resumable handoff view, early prerequisite checks and evidence-based
  reconciliation, citing the owners it relies on with quotes.
- No requirement or gate changes. check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Setup approvals use existing batching, including concrete relay destinations
description:
Interface direction from the review's section 5 ("apply existing setup batching") and the
already-permitted half of review item R07. Wording only: the contract already permits this.

## Current contract

ARC-15: the machine creations a setup names are known before anything starts, so their approvals
batch. For the ordinary dedicated/Robot ceremony, the server host comes from an authenticated,
server-specific Robot read whose returned server number matches the approved machine, recorded with
its source before use. A signed relay destination addition requires approval naming the concrete
host, pass, purpose, source and relationship to the machine; it covers that host on the relay's
any-port terms. Known concrete additions may batch. A host learned later needs a new approval
(ADR-0071 chose concrete approval over authorization tied to the source).

## Change

At the owning clauses (ARC-15 for setup batching; the destination-approval clause in
02-channel.md for relay additions), add clarifying wording that:

- the interface uses existing batching fully: approvals the contract lets share one review are
  presented on one review, not as a sequence of confirmations;
- reconnection to a destination already admitted under an existing approval creates no further
  destination-addition approval, **if and only if** the current text already says so. Verify this
  against the owning clause and quote it. If the current contract in fact requires a new approval on
  reconnection, do not change it: stop and report it as an open question, because changing it would
  be the R07 policy reconsideration that is filed separately for evidence.

## Boundaries

- No authorization by source (ADR-0071 stands). A server host learned later still needs its own
  approval. Host-wide (any-port) scope stays disclosed before authorization.
- No dialing from model text, an account listing or relay metadata. An unresolved addition request
  stays unresolved, with no automatic retransmission.
- This clause does not decide later re-entry or Restore address admission, nor LNVPS manual
  publisher enrollment; do not generalize to those paths.

## Acceptance

- Owning text says permitted approvals share one review; reconnection behavior stated only as the
  contract already has it, with a quote.
- No requirement, ADR or gate weakened. check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Paid inference uses one Start surface and keeps progress visible after expiry
description:
Review item R08, parts A and D (interface improvements the contract already permits; wording
only). Parts B (default duration), C (real-issuer validation) and the locale-decimal amendment are
separate beads.

## Current contract

The offered lifetime is 15 minutes, selectable within 1 to 1440 whole minutes subject to the pinned
issuer profile; the offered cap is 0.10 account units subject to exact support. The operator can
confirm unchanged visible defaults with one Start action; there is no approval per inference
request. The lifetime starts at the fixed issuer-time origin used to authorize minting; delay,
hidden time and suspension consume it. A durable mint intent consumes the session's one attempt,
including refused or uncertain responses. Expiry or cap exhaustion ends the session; a new session
needs its own limits and admission. Only a synthetic fixture profile exists; production minting
stays refused until a real issuer profile is pinned.

## Change

At the owning inference clauses in 01-architecture.md (confirmation, display, expiry) and the
session-expiry clause in 03-state-and-recovery.md, add wording that:

- **A. One Start surface.** The supported cap and duration are shown together, editable in place;
  the primary action confirms those values. The surface explains when time starts and the practical
  meaning of the cap. Internal choice-generation identifiers and clock-evidence mechanics stay out
  of the ordinary decision surface.
- **D. Progress after expiry.** After expiry the interface shows completed work, unresolved
  operations and the next eligible Start action. A new session still needs admission and respects
  outstanding machine-operation holds. Expiry is not evidence that remote work failed.

## Boundaries

- No silent renewal, automatic top-up, second mint within a session, or imputed paid-key expiry for
  BYO/local inference.
- Unsupported defaults stay visibly unavailable, never substituted. No currency symbol or
  affordability claim without an evidenced unit mapping. Fixture-only builds acquire no production
  minting authority.
- Ordinary hide and return keep the same eligible confirmation and original expiry.
- Input grammar is unchanged (locale commas stay refused unless the separate amendment lands).

## Acceptance

- Owning text states A and D as above, quoting the clauses it relies on.
- No limit, grammar, mint-attempt or expiry rule changes. check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Weaker-mode restatement may be concise under the existing policy
description:
Review item R05, first half: concise restatement under the existing SEC-14 policy (already
permitted; wording only). The relevance-based omission half is a separate evidence bead and is not
drafted here.

## Current contract

SEC-14: every standing weaker mode is restated at every later irreversible act on a machine in the
bound set (unpinned installation, jump-host first contact, a goal without a brief, a larger bound
set, an untyped vendor scope); historical exposure can follow the machine into later sessions.
Existing limits: acceptance can occur on a card the interface already shows; one action can both
approve an operation and accept its applicable mode; restatement does not generally mean accepting
the same historical fact again; same-session interruption needs no renewed acceptance.

## Change

At SEC-14 (with pointers only in the secret-placement card, untyped-scope warning and mode
conformance text if they restate presentation), add clarifying wording that restatement may be
concise: a short label per standing mode with its readable consequence on the card, and the full
explanation in expandable detail, with no invented confirmation modal. Every standing mode is still
restated on the card; this changes presentation, not which modes appear.

Verify against SEC-14's exact words that concise labels with expandable detail already satisfy
"restated". If the text forces full explanations on the card, stop and report: that would be the
policy amendment, filed separately.

## Boundaries

- No mode is omitted from the card (that is the separate evidence bead). Initial acceptance and
  acceptance for a newly approved act are unchanged; a new unpinned reinstall still obtains fresh
  acceptance; a failed stronger check still halts instead of falling back.
- Ordinary return to the same eligible session creates no acceptance prompt.
- No risk scorer, relevance mapping or new approval type.

## Acceptance

- SEC-14 states that restatement may take concise per-mode labels with expandable detail, quoting
  the restatement rule it clarifies; dependent texts point at it rather than restating.
- check-all, unit tests and controls green.

title: Restore verification offers a safe retry when evidence is unavailable
description:
Review item R01: offer a safe retry when Restore verification is unavailable. Contract amendment
on the owner's instruction. **Relaxation:** a failed or incomplete verification read with no
contradictory identity evidence no longer forces the reinstall-or-abandon choice. Name this
relaxation in the commit, PR and (if one is written) ADR.

Owners to amend: STA-16 and the applicable CHN-R7 recovery behavior, plus directly dependent
conformance and formal text.

## Current contract

After restoring an active lnvps_retrieve host pin, the harness fetches the vendor's current
published host-key set. A complete set equal to the saved pin permits contact. An empty, partial or
different set, or a failed read, leaves first contact unresolved as though the maximum wait has
passed; the specified choices are reinstall or abandonment. The read itself does not retire the
pin. This joins two situations: evidence unavailable (timeout, publication not complete) and
evidence contradicting the saved identity (a newly observed conflicting fingerprint).

## Change

Offer another authorized verification read when the missing evidence can be collected by the
existing permitted read. Keep the saved pin, installation boundaries, publication observations and
unresolved status intact; contact stays withheld until the original checks pass. Candidate text for
the owning clause:

> A failed or incomplete verification read that supplies no contradictory identity evidence MUST
> NOT, by itself, require reinstall or abandonment. The interface MUST permit another authorized
> verification read while retaining the saved pin and all publication observations. Contact remains
> withheld until the existing pin, publication-history and installation checks admit it. Retrying a
> read neither opens an installation nor authorizes a mutation.

## Boundaries

- Narrow to revalidation of an already admitted, restored pin; does not reopen initial first
  contact without a previously admitted pin.
- An incomplete response containing a conflicting fingerprint is contradictory evidence, retained.
  A later matching response must not erase evidence the installation-history rules require the
  harness to consider. A complete mismatch keeps the existing identity hold.
- No accepting a replacement key, deleting observations, or treating a timeout as proof nothing
  happened remotely. Destructive recovery stays a separately explained choice.
- No general recovery workflow engine: one recovery transition using the existing reader.
- If STA-16 or CHN-R7 is formalized, change the Lean declaration with the Markdown; never weaken a
  theorem to make it pass. If the amendment would touch a theorem, gate or assumption boundary
  beyond what it needs, stop and report.

## Acceptance (focused checks)

- A transport failure followed by a qualifying matching publication restores contact without
  reinstall.
- An incomplete response with no conflicting fingerprint keeps retry available and admits no
  contact.
- A conflicting observation survives retry, restart and replay; a later response cannot silently
  erase it.
- Retry sends only the authorized verification read: no reinstall, new installation or mutation
  retry. A failed append of required evidence leaves contact withheld.
- Conformance covers these with applicability and tier metadata where new items are added.
  check-all, unit tests and controls green.

comments.text:
Restore failed-append panel, two rounds on the blocked Run's snapshot (9e1a4d1), accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule. Four readers answered each round; the fifth seat was missing (out of credit), so it does not count.

Round one (question: does a failed append of required evidence during Restore revalidation mean a lasting machine-wide stop, or only withholding under the restored pin?):
- Core B, 4 of 4: a failed append of required evidence withholds contact under the restored pin and leaves its revalidation unresolved. Destructive recovery (ARC-22) and the next installation's first contact (CHN-R7) stay with their existing owners. The never-cleared machine-wide marker verificationAppendFailed and the theorem restore_failed_storage_not_bypassed_by_reinstall go.
- 4 of 4: under STA-3 ("If the append fails, the transition does not occur") an observation whose append failed is not canonical harness knowledge. Durably appended observations stay in every later CHN-R7 comparison.
- 4 of 4: SEC-11's "nothing stored to check against", and the no_pin row in the witness format document, say that a restored pin can be stored but not eligible for contact.
- 4 of 4: add one targeted negative control for each new Restore guard: restoreBeforeContact, restoreReadAuthorized, restoreSavedPin and restoreEvidenceDurable.

Round two (the three points round one left split or open):
- Formal shape N (plain no-op), 3 of 4: on a failed required append, verifyRestored returns the knowledge unchanged, as TauWeb.Dispatch.append and this module's failed attest append already do. The standing pendingVerification entry is the restored-pin hold. No new proof boundary. verificationAppendFailed leaves Knowledge, pinFor, offersVerification, the witness knowledge table and the assumption text, which take the attest wording: a failed append records nothing, so the next authorized read can still succeed. The dissent preferred an explicit proof boundary that ends the represented history at the failed append.
- Retry stays, 3 of 4: the state after a failed append is the pre-read state, which STA-16's retry sentence covers. Another authorized verification read stays available (offersVerification true), also after a contradictory read whose append failed. The dissent could not tell from the text.
- Conformance item 84, 4 of 4: restate. Its sentence "a subsequent matching read cannot bypass the unrecorded required evidence to release contact" has no owning requirement (STA-16's "that evidence" is retained evidence) and goes. The restated item: the failed append of a conflicting partial observation leaves contact withheld, including after restart and replay; the saved pin and recorded history are unchanged; another authorized verification read is offered. restore_failed_conflict_stays_withheld drops its matching step after the failure and claims the knowledge after the failed append equals the knowledge before the read, with no session and offersVerification true. Both changed theorems are new in this amendment; no theorem on main changes.

Narrowing and widening:
- Narrowing of this bead's acceptance line "A conflicting observation survives retry, restart and replay": it holds for a durably appended observation. A contradiction whose append failed is not retained, so a later qualifying read can release contact under the restored pin. The companion already leaves the same exposure outside itself for an ordinary CHN-R7 publication whose append fails. Making an unrecorded contradiction count anyway would be a new rule that no panel has read; it is not drafted.
- Widening: STA-16's retry duty reaches the state after a failed required append, not only a failed or incomplete read.
- Narrowing of the blocked Run's draft only, not of this bead: its lasting machine-wide stop becomes withholding under the restored pin.

title: Ad-hoc machines default to the conservative class
description:
Review item R02: default ad-hoc machines to the conservative class. Contract amendment on the
owner's instruction. **Relaxation:** the mandatory up-front classification questions for an ad-hoc
machine are no longer asked when the conservative (multi-tenant) class supports the whole task.
Name this relaxation in the commit, PR and ADR. It partly reverses ADR-0034's recorded decision
("*Machine class* is asked. … The questions are the harness's, nothing is preselected, and an
operator who is not sure has a multi-tenant machine"): record that in a new ADR superseding that
part (do not rewrite ADR-0034's history). ADR-0034's rejection of "Have the model propose the machine
class and the operator approve it" stays in force: the default is the harness's, never the model's.

Owners to amend: ARC-36a, the ad-hoc tenant profile, and directly affected conformance cases.

## Current contract

For a machine without a tenant preset, the operator answers harness-authored classification
questions with nothing preselected; the model cannot answer or preselect them. An uncertain answer
selects multi-tenant, which forbids spendable key material (ARC-37) and requires the machine to be
bound alone. The spec itself says these restrictions do not affect a one-machine task that needs no
wallet. Multi-tenant here means serving parties the operator has never met (ARC-36), not sharing
physical hardware.

## Change

For initial ad-hoc admission, use the conservative class without a separate question when the task
can proceed within its restrictions; record that the class came from a harness default, not an
operator assertion. Ask the signed questions only before a requested capability needs a less
restrictive class. Candidate text:

> For an ad-hoc machine, the harness MAY assign the conservative multi-tenant class by default and
> record that provenance. A default is not an operator answer. Before admitting behavior that
> requires a less restrictive class, the harness MUST obtain an explicit operator answer to the
> signed classification questions. The model MUST NOT supply or relax that answer.

## Boundaries

- Tenant presets keep their treatment. No unrestricted reclassification mechanism for
  already-bound machines (state whether and how the existing question path applies before a
  relaxing capability is admitted; if the text forces a design choice here, stop and report).
- All multi-tenant restrictions hold under the default, including the secret-placement
  confirmation that a value is not spendable on a multi-tenant machine.
- Model text, restored UI state or a previously displayed suggestion cannot manufacture an operator
  answer. No policy-inference subsystem: one default provenance plus the existing question path.

## Acceptance (focused checks)

- A normal one-machine, no-wallet goal reaches setup approval without an obligatory classification
  screen.
- The default retains all multi-tenant restrictions.
- A request requiring relaxed restrictions cannot proceed without the signed operator question.
- Model text, restored state or a displayed suggestion cannot manufacture an answer.

title: Decide retired-seed handoffs and a pending migration index at a later Replace
description:
tw-1wq's text (ADR-0058) leaves two retired-seed points open, both named in the credential format's payload version 7.

**Handoffs.** The format says "What the new seed's sheet holds for a handoff allocated under a retired seed is not yet specified". `retired_allocations` admits only the families `machine` and `pass`, and `STA-22b`'s journal-keep list names no handoff.

**A pending migration index at a later Replace.** The format says "neither is what a later Replace does with a `migration_index` whose reserved allocation is under the seed that Replace retires". A `migration_index` must name a machine allocation in the current `allocations`. After a failed relabel read the machine keeps its retired-seed name and its new index stays reserved; a second Replace retires the seed that reservation was made under, so the export has no current allocation to name. `STA-17`'s direct re-entry ("a dedicated machine counts as migrated only when a read shows the new id") and the reserved key that may already be on the machine both bear on it. A Failed tombstone does not fit: `STA-22b` says "Failed requires local proof that this allocation's create was never sent".

Until both are written, a Replace export in either case can fail its own import (`CNF-84`: "no export can write a sheet its own import refuses").
close_reason: Retired-seed handoffs and pending migration indexes specified in payload version 7 (ADR-0059).

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Pick — a retired-seed handoff stays under its seed; a pending migration index is read first, then superseded, 2026-11-05

Accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 rule ("if 4/4 agree, just accept it"). One reader seat was unavailable; four of four readers agree on both parts.

**Handoffs: keep it under its retired seed.** The new seed's sheet carries each handoff the journal keeps under a retired seed in `retired_allocations`, family `handoff`, with its seed, index, tenant and handoff ID, recorded public key and `outstanding` with a closed reason, for as long as its declared lifetime runs. The post-harness machinery is given the credential only after the harness derives it from the retired seed the operator supplies and compares it with the recorded key. Using it is a step that needs the retired seed, so Replace's screen says the retired seed stays needed for it. The entry ends in one journal act when the journal records the profile's declared end. Replace does not re-issue a handoff: its public half is installed only during setup, over the bound session's channel, and a sealed machine cannot be told a new key.

**Pending migration index: read first, else supersede it.** When a later Replace re-enters a machine whose migration index is under the seed that Replace retires, it first takes the label read `STA-17` already requires. A read showing the reserved index's id confirms that migration in one journal act, and the machine then migrates like any machine of that seed. Otherwise the machine keeps its own retired-seed entry and gets a fresh migration index under the new seed, and the old reservation becomes its own retired machine entry: `outstanding` with reason `"superseded_reservation"`, linked to the machine's entry. Like a migration index, it is not a second machine: no record names it, and it has no machine state or artifact history. Its recorded key is one more retired public key that re-entry removes from the machine. The act that migrates or destroys the machine also ends its superseded reservations. A third Replace copies them unchanged.

The text forces neither part: four of four. It does exclude two options. Re-issuing a handoff under the new seed conflicts with "during setup, before the handoff point" and "over the bound session's own channel". Dropping the reservation conflicts with "Failed requires local proof that this allocation's create was never sent", given the reserved key was installed. Once a read shows the reserved id, `STA-17`'s "A later read showing the new id confirms the relabel without another write" decides that branch.

**What these picks widen or amend, named:**

- 113000001's "`retired_allocations` carrying every allocation the journal keeps under an earlier seed" covers handoffs too, beyond machine and pass entries; the recorded-key acceptance, deferred to before use, covers a retired handoff.
- `STA-17`'s "needs its backup *during* Replace and abandons it after" and `SEC-5` row 15's "until the last step that needs it is done": a retired-seed handoff's use, while its lifetime runs, is such a step.
- 113000001's "the reserved index is linked, not a second machine" gains a second linked kind, the superseded reservation; the format's "the one repeated mapping import accepts" widens to it.
- `CNF-84` (BLOCKING): import accepts family `handoff`, the new machine reason and the link member, and refuses their malformed forms.

**Not selected:** for handoffs, re-issuing under the new seed where a channel remains, and ending the handoff at Replace; for the pending index, re-entering without the read, and dropping the reservation.

**Version.** This amends payload version 7, as 113000001 did; its text marks both points not yet specified, and nothing in the repository writes a version-7 sheet.

**What the text work must write in:** the credential format's version-7 text (family, handoff reason, superseded reservation and link, import checks, exporter rule); `STA-22b`'s keep list; `STA-17`'s Replace export paragraph and backup sentence; `SEC-5` row 15; `CNF-84`; ADR-0058's open points, closed by a new ADR.

This owner decision is settled and must not be re-asked. It makes no normative edit by itself and no capability, readiness or runtime claim.

title: Decide whether the LNVPS recovery row owes CNF evidence for the deletion reader's Replace half
description:
The LNVPS path's recovery row in `07-conformance.md` ("The LNVPS path: recovery export/import and Replace") requires the Replace cases before maintained-cloud delivery. It also says the dedicated, model-free deletion reader (`tw-ae7` comment 60000001) is specified, and that its scope over the old machine of an LNVPS Replace rebuild applies wherever LNVPS Replace is offered. No CNF item names the reader, so nothing in that row requires evidence of the reader's Replace half.

## Question

Is integrated evidence of the reader's Replace half owed before LNVPS Replace is offered, and if so, which CNF item carries it (a case in an existing recovery item, or a new item with its row)?

## Bounds

- Raised during the stage removal (`tw-o6r`) and deliberately kept out of that edit.
- Do not narrow or widen the recovery row in the meantime. The reader's unfinished-setup half stays with the in-setup replacement order's row ("Before enabling the in-setup replacement order at LNVPS"), which reads "none yet".
- Whether "unfinished setup" covers an abandoned setup still waiting on M's deletion is a separate open question; this bead does not answer it.
- Related: `tw-ae7` comments 60000001 and 68000001.
close_reason: Landed decision 91000001 in 07-conformance.md: CNF-20 gains the deletion check's Replace-use case and CNF-26 its abandonment-use case, each with scope, no-automatic-start, no-key and no-session/SSH-key/model refusals. The recovery row requires CNF-20's case before the check is offered for a machine Replace's flow stopped, and the LNVPS delivery row requires CNF-26's case before it is offered for a machine the abandonment flow stopped; each use is gated by its own case, the in-setup rung's machine stays with the in-setup order's row, and neither case is required before delivery. T44's gate is kept. Specified, not enabled; runtime remains outstanding.

title: Does anything hold a restored machine whose pre-loss command may still be running?
description:
## Decision — journal-only, 2026-11-01

The owner chose journal-only protection. Add no recovery check or hold for commands absent from the restored journal. New work after recovery, including Replace's model-free key migration, may overlap an earlier command the restored journal does not record. Intents without terminal records that a backup does retain still hold under the existing journal-derived rules. Other admission checks and standing restrictions remain in force.

## Why this issue exists

A machine can keep running a command after the phone loses the journal that recorded its send. A sheet contains no outstanding-call record. An imported local-store backup differs from total journal loss: it may retain some unresolved intents, while omitting later sends. The original question's claim that nothing journaled holds every restored machine was too broad for that backup case.

`STA-24` states "The barrier is a fact of the journal — an intent with no terminal record" and "What this rule cannot reach is a journal that is lost with the phone: `STA-14` states that transcripts are gone, and a recovery sheet is not an outstanding-call record." `STA-20` records jobs "on persistent disk (`/var/lib/tau-web/jobs`, root-only)" and says "On the installed system the files survive a reboot". Those surviving machine records do not recreate a lost journal intent.

`STA-21` states "The job record is machine-reported and advisory." Enumeration cannot reveal commands that left no record, prove completeness against a hostile machine or reconstruct approvals. This limit must not be presented as a new concurrency guarantee.

## Triage outcome

Astra and Sol recommended a bounded recovery guard. Opus recommended an operator-cancellable advisory wait. Fable was a missing seat because of its usage limit; Grok was a missing seat because of HTTP 402 balance exhaustion. The owner explicitly rejected those recommendations in favor of journal-only. The structured brief in this issue's comments records the decision, the still-binding constraints and the acceptance criteria.

## Closes when

The owning `STA-20` command-hold text and `STA-24` lost-journal limit explicitly describe this boundary, including overlap during Replace, without bypassing any retained unresolved intent or standing restriction. Preserve advisory evidence, existing collection and all other admission rules. The amendment must not weaken any existing theorem, gate, requirement or assumption boundary. No recovery guard, advisory wait or new dispatch exception is part of this outcome.

Found by the 2026-10-18 grill (tw-k12). The issue remains open for the bounded specification clarification; no normative amendment or integrated result is claimed by triage.

Carry forward `STA-21`'s "The job record is machine-reported and advisory." Enumeration cannot reveal commands that left no record. The amendment must preserve existing theorems, gates, requirements and assumption boundaries. It clarifies journal knowledge, not remote concurrency safety, and creates no synthetic intent, approval or terminal evidence.

No further owner policy question remains for this clarification. Category bug; open and ready-for-agent for specification editing. The comment's amendment brief supplies acceptance criteria. Live/integrated evidence and the actual normative edit remain outstanding.

**Owner decision — 2026-11-01:**
Journal-only. Add no recovery-time record-enumeration check, advisory wait or hold for commands absent from the restored journal. New work after recovery, including model commands, harness-composed check/delivery jobs and Replace's model-free key migration, may overlap an earlier command the restored journal does not record. This is a limit of the chosen protection, not a claim that overlap is safe or that all other admission checks pass.

**Panel split recorded with the decision:**
- Astra: a bounded recovery collection-and-hold guard, to catch observable unfinished work before another command overlaps it.
- Sol: a bounded recovery guard; the restored machine's unchecked state supplies no command-concurrency protection.
- Opus: an operator-cancellable advisory wait; a machine-reported or forged running record must not indefinitely prevent replacing a stolen key.
- Fable: missing seat because of its usage limit.
- Grok: missing seat because of HTTP 402 balance exhaustion.

The owner chose journal-only against those recommendations. This is the owner's decision, not a panel consensus. No guard or advisory-wait design branch remains authorized by this issue.

**Current behavior and the gap to clarify:**
`STA-24` states "The barrier is a fact of the journal — an intent with no terminal record" and "What this rule cannot reach is a journal that is lost with the phone: `STA-14` states that transcripts are gone, and a recovery sheet is not an outstanding-call record." Its current command-hold interpretation likewise derives from surviving intents. The command-hold text needs the corresponding recovery limit made explicit, without weakening that hold for any intent that does survive.

Distinguish total journal loss from an imported local-store backup. A stale backup may retain unresolved intents, terminal records and standing dispositions; the surviving restrictions remain in force. It can also omit later sends. A terminal record collected for one retained intent establishes nothing about another command omitted from the backup. Recovery does not settle a retained unresolved intent, clear its barrier or erase a standing restriction.

**Requirement owners and binding limits:**
- `STA-20` owns the command hold and permitted collection: "Collecting a job record is not held, and other machines are unaffected." State the journal-only limit beside the hold, and point to the existing lost-journal boundary at `STA-24`. Preserve ordinary collection for known calls; rejecting a new recovery-wide check does not remove or prohibit existing permitted reads.
- `STA-8` requires "It MUST NOT be retried automatically and no timer may clear it." `STA-24` supplies the resource barrier and disposition rules. Keep these unchanged for every retained unresolved intent and standing restriction.
- `STA-17` owns Replace. It requires "A machine under `STA-20`'s hold or a standing destructive reinstall or abandonment disposition (`STA-24`) MUST be shown as not yet migrated, with the reason, and MUST keep its old key; Replace migrates the others." Clarify that the absence of a lost intent supplies no additional hold; it does not grant an exemption from a surviving hold or change key-install/confirmation/removal ordering.
- `STA-21` states "The job record is machine-reported and advisory." It also states "The browser journal is authoritative for what was **sent** (`STA-3`, `ARC-8`); the machine's record says what it **received** and what happened next." Retain that boundary. Machine-side enumeration cannot reveal commands that left no record, establish completeness against a hostile machine, reconstruct lost intents or approvals, or promise that an old phone cannot send further work.
- Existing recovery presentation and re-check requirements retain their owners. Explain the chosen overlap limit where recovery and Replace are presented, by referring to its normative owner rather than copying a new rule into several homes. Being unchecked after recovery does not supply the rejected enumeration guard.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The owning command-hold and lost-journal text explicitly states journal-only protection and distinguishes full journal loss from an imported backup retaining some unresolved intents.
- [ ] The text explicitly says that new work after recovery, including Replace's model-free key migration, may overlap an earlier command whose send the restored journal does not record. It makes no new concurrency-safety or remote-completeness claim.
- [ ] Every surviving unresolved intent still has its existing hold, reconciliation and disposition behavior. An absent later intent does not release a retained intent or a standing destructive restriction, and settlement of one retained call says nothing about omitted sends.
- [ ] There is no new recovery enumeration prerequisite, advisory wait, orphan-record hold, synthetic intent/approval, new terminal evidence or automatic retry. Existing permitted collection and other admission/output-release checks remain intact.
- [ ] The advisory-record boundary and the inability to discover commands with no record remain explicit. Retain the selected sudo route and its missing-record uncertainty from tw-yuo without turning that route into a recovery check.
- [ ] Check the explanation against the existing journal-derived `openIntents`, command hold and retained-intent/recovery conformance cases. Make only the references or focused coverage needed to demonstrate the chosen boundary; do not invent a conformance guard for the rejected policy.
- [ ] Preserve every existing theorem, gate, requirement and assumption boundary. A theorem is not weakened to make the overlap explanation pass; the explanation must state the knowledge limit the existing guard already has. No new engine or dispatch exception is authorized.
- [ ] Land the rule before recording the rationale, record the rejected guard and advisory-wait alternatives without creating a second normative copy, and run the repository's required gates before and after the amendment. Any new conformance case receives its proper applicability row and tier metadata.

**Readiness and boundaries:**
No further owner policy question remains for this bounded clarification. Keep the issue open and ready-for-agent for specification editing. This triage does not implement the normative amendment or establish live/integrated recovery evidence. Recovery-guard design, new job identity/schema machinery, vendor/machine operations and changes to existing admission or settlement semantics are outside this amendment.

title: OPN-14: does re-entry read running-at-delivery services, and does that lifecycle bind after delivery?
description:
## The question

`OPN-14` leaves two points open:

- "whether `STG-9`'s re-entry re-check reads `running-at-delivery` services, and whether a stopped
  one is then outside its declared lifecycle and hence a lifecycle finding (`CNF-108`)";
- "Whether `running-at-delivery` binds after delivery remains open."

`OPN-14` frames the second: "`ARC-17` says "whenever that read runs — at a delivery check or a
later re-check"; the open point is when that declared lifecycle applies after delivery."

## Why it matters now

`OPN-14` "does block completing the first stage", and the stage-1 re-entry row requires item 108
"before stage 1 completes". Re-entry reads for `enabled-survives-reboot` services are decided:
`ARC-43` says "On re-entry (`STG-9`), read the unit and its enablement for
`enabled-survives-reboot` services." The implementation builds those now. The rest waits as twr-ggw.73, behind the pin
bump twr-ggw.35, and cannot be written until these two points are decided.

## Closes when

Both points are decided in the text that owns them, `OPN-14` no longer lists them as open, and
`T42` agrees.
close_reason: Landed ARC-43 re-entry read and boot anchor, ARC-17 lifecycle findings, OPN-14/T42 and ADR-0049

title: CNF-109's admission from the job-read and attest routes at stage 1, which has neither
description:
## The question

`CNF-109` is in the stage-1 required row ("109–110") with no carve-out. Two of its sentences need
a route stage 1 does not have: a new job-read pin needs the dedicated path's rescue job, and a new
attest pin needs the attest route:

- "a new valid published, job-read, or unused eligible attest introduction can pin under its own
  rules"
- "A consumed attest introduction stays consumed."

Stage 1 has no attest route: the row says items 18 and 61 "remain route-specific attest checks,
required before enabling that route, not stage-1 requirements". A stage-1 harness can hold an
attest pin as history (Restore round-trips "an initial empty group opened by a job read or attest"
and "the active or retired status of pins from each source", `CNF-84`), so the history cases of
`CNF-109` are owed at stage 1. Proving that a consumed introduction "stays consumed" needs a later
attest attempt, which only the attest route can make.

Decided 2026-10-15 (owner): item 109's admission of a new job-read pin is the dedicated row's;
its admission of an unused attest introduction, and a consumed introduction staying consumed, are
the attest row's, as item 23's attest-window case already is. Stage 1 keeps the cases against
earlier job-read and attest pins, on pins a Restore brings in.

The implementation's companion comparison of `pins-witnesses-v4.json` leaves the 16 witnesses
holding an `attest` step (and 2246 enumerated traces) unreplayed at stage 1 until this is
answered, and its stage-1 admission record lists them by name as pending.

## Done when

The stage-1 row, or `CNF-109`, says where these two sentences apply, on the spec's main.
close_reason: Applicability rows now assign each route-specific case to its route, retaining restored history at stage 1.

The stage-1 row retains restored job-read and attest history cases. CNF-109 text unchanged.

title: LNVPS operations have no confirmation predicate (restart, stop, renewal-off, reinstall, deletion)
description:
## The gap

`STA-24`: "Evidence is the observation the operation's own reconciliation contract admits — for
Robot, `STG-4`'s predicates". `STG-4` and the rules after it define those predicates for Robot only.
No requirement defines the observation that confirms any LNVPS operation: the typed restart, the stop
that stands in for a destroy, renewal-off, or the vendor's reinstall call.

So at LNVPS each of those calls stays unresolved until the operator disposes of it, and while one
that changes what the machine is running (`STA-24`) is unresolved, box-plane dispatch to the
machine stays stopped. Duties resting on the missing contract:
- `ARC-43`: the opted-in delivery restart, "with its own vendor confirmation under `STA-24`";
  "Until that confirmation, box-plane dispatch stays stopped." (the boot-identity read is never
  the restart's confirmation).
- `STA-24`: "At LNVPS renewal-off waits for the stop's confirmation".
- `STA-24`: the reinstall continuation at LNVPS is dispatched at "the vendor's reinstall call";
  its confirmation closes the restriction's successor barrier.
- The implementation's LNVPS tickets (stop and renewal-off; reinstall, "confirmed only by the
  predicate the spec pin carries").

## The question

For each of the four operations, what observation — from LNVPS's machine status read
(`GET /api/v1/vm/{id}`, `VmStatus`), its published host keys, or a box-plane read where `STA-24`
allows one — confirms it, what is merely "ended", and what leaves it unresolved? Ground it in the
2026-10-08 LNVPS research and the 2026-10-11 phase B observations.

Found by the 2026-10-16 contradiction pass over branch docs/grill-1015.

The vendor's deletion of a stopped machine needs a confirming observation beside those of the four harness operations. `SEC-5` rows 12 and 23 count it as the machine's destruction at LNVPS: "the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop that stands in for a destroy"; that deletion observation is owed here too. The starting fact in `docs/findings/2026-10-11-lnvps-phase-b.md` is "A stop (`PATCH …/stop`) left the machine `stopped` and still listed, with `deleting_on` one day after the expiry (the grace may lengthen with the subscription's age; it was read at day 0)." No deletion has been observed. The observation has to work for a machine whose vendor key went with a retired or missing seed (`STA-17`); without one, that machine's placed secrets stay listed for good.
close_reason: T50 specified in STA-5, STA-24, STG-21/STG-21a and CNF-112: narrow exact-call receipts, unique-match order reconciliation, renewal/reinstall/deletion reads and account verification/reissue. ADR-0042 and TRU-E1 record accepted administrative-transfer risk and the deferred reappearance billing-display gap. Lost-key duties remain; no operator-carried evidence path. Specification closure only; no live deletion or implementation claim.

title: Does a destructive disposition stop a box-plane job the harness starts on its own?
description:
## The question

While a disposition naming a destructive reinstall or abandonment stands on a machine, is a
box-plane job the harness starts on its own (`delivery_reboot`, `digest_secret`, the delivery
check's harness-composed reads, `replace_root_label`) refused, or dispatched?

## What the text says

- `STA-24`: "the harness worker MUST refuse the model's box-plane commands to that machine,
  whatever the disposed call was. A harness-owned job the model requests (`ARC-43`) is one of
  them". Harness-initiated jobs are not named.
- `STA-24`: "a disposed box-plane command restricts only what an unresolved box-plane command
  bars", and "Box-plane dispatch to the machine is governed by `STA-20` and `STA-20b`, not by
  this rule". `STA-20`'s hold (2026-10-18, ADR-0048) is released by any disposition, so it is
  not part of a disposition's reach.
- `STA-24`: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane".
- ADR-0044 rejected "A destructive continuation adds nothing beyond what the disposed call
  barred" because "A stray command would pre-empt the reinstall the operator chose".

`TauWeb.Dispatch` follows the text: under a standing destructive reinstall disposition of a
command, a `deliveryReboot` request is dispatched, stays unresolved, and its barrier refuses
the reinstall's rescue activation until its boot change is collected.

## Readings

- A: the destructive stop covers every box-plane job, harness-initiated ones included; only
  reads and the collection of job records pass.
- B: as written today; a harness-initiated job runs under a destructive continuation and can
  pre-empt the reinstall.

## Closes when

`STA-24` says which reading holds for harness-initiated jobs, and `TauWeb.Dispatch` agrees.
close_reason: STA-24 stops every box-plane job; ARC-43 paste at once; STA-17; CNF-95/CNF-110; TauWeb.Dispatch.stops; ADR-0050

title: Decide what ends a failed rotation attempt's new placement, and what a failed first placement does
description:
tw-38p (ADR-0063) records a rotation only when the act admits the rotation job's completed
root-only job record with a zero exit. Until then the new placement is listed, and its reference
required, from the record made before its bytes leave. This bead asks what ends that new placement
when the rotation is never recorded, and what a failed first placement does.

**What the text says.**
- `SEC-5`: "The record made before the bytes leave (`ARC-8`), a nonzero exit, a job that stays
  unresolved (`STA-8`) and a disposition (`STA-24`) record no rotation".
- `ARC-43`: "A rotation's new placement is listed from the record made before its bytes leave,
  whatever its job then does".
- The credential format writes a rotation's new placement only once `SEC-5` records the rotation,
  so a Restore ends a failed attempt's new placement.

**The gap.**
- After a nonzero exit, an unresolved job or a disposition, while the local store stays intact,
  the new placement stays listed and its reference required with no act that ends it. A later
  rotation attempt of P adds another.
- A first placement (no old placement) whose job exits nonzero, stays unresolved or is disposed:
  the text does not say whether it is listed, whether its reference is required, or whether the
  export writes it.

**Questions.**
1. What ends a failed rotation attempt's new placement, its listing and its required reference: a
   later recorded rotation, destruction, an operator act, or nothing?
2. What does a failed first placement do to its listing, its reference and the export?

Constraints that hold either way:
- `STA-4`: a call with an intent and no terminal record "may have been sent, never that it was not".
- `STA-24`: a disposition keeps the outcome unknown.
- The credential format's duplicate rule for records without a report at one machine, application
  name, secret name and path.
- No raw value, bare digest or scan key enters history or export.

Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.
close_reason: First-placement starts and export, completed-attempt retirement, and retained disposed predecessors are specified in ARC-43, SEC-5/6, the credential format and CNF-95(l)/(m), with ADR-0069/0070; one review pass applied. Specification closure only.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
## Partial decision — failed placements, 2026-11-06

Four independent readers answered; a fifth seat was unavailable. The shared cores below are
accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule. The recommendations' headings agreed, but a
substantive exception in their bodies prevents treating the whole rotation question as settled.

**Accepted: first-placement listing and reference, 4 of 4.** A first placement is listed and its
reference required from the approved record made before its bytes leave, whatever its job then
does. A nonzero exit, an unresolved job or a disposition ends neither. A late completed record
of a disposed call does not change that start. This fills the first-placement gap ADR-0063 left
open; it does not move a rotation attempt's existing start or make failure evidence of absence.

**Accepted: first-placement export, 4 of 4, independently of the preceding choice.** A first
placement enters the sheet from that pre-send record, even when its job is unsuccessful. A later
placement at the same machine, application name, secret name and path is a rotation there, even
if the first job never succeeded. The later attempt keeps the existing rotation export delay.
For a completed first attempt followed by a recorded rotation, the new record replaces the
first placement's unreported record; the importer still refuses two such records at the tuple.
This settles first-placement inventory previously left open. It does not reverse ADR-0063's
exclusion of an unrecorded rotation attempt. The disposed-predecessor replacement case below is
held, not silently decided by this export choice.

**Accepted rotation core, 4 of 4.** A later recorded rotation ends earlier still-live unreported
attempts at exactly the same machine, application name, secret name and path when their completed
root-only job records were admitted before that later rotation's pre-send record. Earlier means
pre-send journal order, never a timestamp, value comparison, digest or machine claim. The common
case is a nonzero completed attempt followed by a zero-exit recorded rotation. Each additionally
ended placement uses the existing rotation scan boundary, wait retirement, mark and no-revocation
limits. The card names the placements it ends. Reported history and other tuples remain separate.

This widens what one recorded rotation ends under ADR-0063/0061, shortens those additional
references' lifetime at that boundary, and extends ADR-0060's mark to their ends, including when
the original placement was reported. ADR-0061's withholding boundary and ADR-0064's card/display
warning apply to every additionally ended value. It does not weaken withholding, make rotation
revocation or erasure, extend a report beyond its own placement, or change ADR-0062/0067/0068.
No sheet field, schema version, importer rule, theorem or formal declaration changes.

**Held for the owner: disposed attempts without an admitted completed record before the next
pre-send, 3 to 1.** Three would end them with the later recorded rotation as well; one would
retain their references until a completed record precedes a later attempt, because the disposed
job could still write after the replacement. The minority is the reader the panel rule requires
for a non-unanimous acceptance. This is a semantic difference, not wording. If the retained attempt
is the first placement and is on the sheet, that recommendation also delays exporting its
successor until the retained attempt ends; the majority replaces the first record normally.
No decision is recorded for this case.

**Other details are not accepted by this record.** Two readers propose exporting a reported
failed rotation attempt despite ADR-0063's no-sheet rule; two do not propose that exception and
treat an unarmed never-exported attempt as unreachable with the intact store. There is no shared
core for that additional export amendment. A proposed extra display label and a separate older
conformance-wording concern also have no panel decision. These remain separate from the accepted
cores and from the one owner question above.

The bead stays open until its held question and text work are complete. This record makes no
capability, readiness or runtime claim.

comments.text:
## Partial implementation and review — failed-placement cores, 2026-11-06

The accepted behavioral cores in comment 142000001 are now text in `ARC-43`, `SEC-5`,
`SEC-6`, the credential format, `CNF-95(l)` and `(m)`, with ADR-0069 recording the decision.
The disposed-predecessor split stays open on this bead; no outcome is chosen for it.

One review pass ran with two independent readers. Both found that the generic P-end and
sheet-replacement sentences could silently choose the held outcome for a disposed first
placement. Those sentences are now explicitly qualified for that case, whether the
disposed placement is P or an additional predecessor. One review also found the approval
race: a completed job record admitted after card approval can change the set the later
rotation ends. `ARC-43` now rechecks that set before send, refuses transmission on a changed
set and composes a new card. The conformance case exercises that race and its refusal control.
Both findings were applied once, without another review.

The same pass tightened the scan-limit citation, the failed-first mark and early-export
controls, the nonzero-attempt wording, the box-plane hold wording, the late disposed-record
start rule and ADR-0063's pointer.

**Count clarification for comment 142000001:** card-naming is separate from the unanimous
behavioral cores. Three readers explicitly recommended naming the placements the rotation
would end; the fourth did not address it. This is accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05
panel rule, with the required reader among those recommending it. No silent answer is
counted as an affirmative vote. ADR-0069 now records that separate count. This corrects
the implication of unanimity for card-naming in the earlier record, without changing the
unanimous cores or the held split.

`tw-x7k` remains open. The owner is being asked whether a later recorded rotation also ends
a disposed predecessor whose completed root-only record was not admitted before the later
pre-send record, including that first placement's successor export. Its answer belongs in
a later change. No schema, importer, theorem or formal declaration is changed, and this
record makes no capability, readiness or runtime claim. Full publication-head gates run

comments.text:
## Round-two decision — retain the possibly unfinished predecessor, 2026-11-06

Packet SHA-256: 1d4e96829d558bb152058237bcda19e572fd6952c2bb5d4768058ec6799ed2bf.
Four independent readers answered, each citing that full hash; a fifth seat was unavailable.
The owner requested another panel, not a policy pick. This record is the round-two tally,
separate from the first-round record 142000001 and its partial implementation in 143000001.

**Core NARROW: 4 of 4, accepted under the owner's 2026-11-05 panel rule.** A later recorded
rotation does not end a same-destination placement whose call the journal records as disposed
and whose completed root-only job record was not admitted before the later rotation's approved
pre-send record. This applies whether that predecessor is P, an additional earlier attempt,
or the first placement there. The predecessor stays listed and its reference required; a
later eligible rotation whose pre-send follows completed-record admission can end it. Its
existing destruction and unarmed-only report ends keep their terms.

**First-placement sheet consequence: 4 of 4, accepted under the same rule.** A retained first
placement keeps the sheet's one unreported record at that destination and delays its otherwise
exportable successor's export until the first placement ends. The successor still stays
listed and required locally. This can omit a locally known successful successor even from
a sheet exported after its zero-exit record. A Restore then restores only the first placement
and re-arms it from the path's current bytes; it recovers neither the omitted successor's
identity nor distinct scan coverage for both historical values. The existing destruction,
reported-history and importer rules still apply; no sheet exports two unreported records
at the same machine, application name, secret name and path.

**Why the earlier split converged.** A continuing disposition does not prove the older job
finished. That job can write its value after the later rotation completes. A newly dispatched
job that reads the file must still meet the retained reference's scan; merely preserving
pre-rotation withheld output would not cover it. The same-file replacement argument applies
to a predecessor known completed before the later pre-send, not necessarily to this writer.
The previously accepted completed-before-pre-send core remains unchanged.

Completed-record admission after pre-send, whether before or after the later zero-exit
admission, never enlarges that rotation's fixed end set retroactively. A disposed call's
own late completed record records no rotation. A new eligible rotation can use it once its
admission precedes that new pre-send. The existing approval-card set recheck remains.

**Narrowings and widenings named.** This resolves ADR-0069's open case. Against ADR-0063's
older generic P-end and sheet-replacement language, it narrows which predecessor ends and
widens the successor-export omission from an unrecorded rotation's window to a recorded
successful rotation whose first predecessor remains required. An admitted rotation may end
no predecessor and set no mark. ADR-0068's armed-placement explanation must qualify which
rotation ends that placement. These are semantic choices, not merely wording fixes.
No retained predecessor sets a mark; each placement actually ended keeps ADR-0060/0061's
mark and withholding boundary. ADR-0062's final unarmed-only report and ADR-0064's no-revocation
and no-erasure limits remain. No disposition, digest, refusal, failed append or late record
becomes evidence of non-execution or adds retry authority. No schema, importer, theorem or
formal declaration is weakened or changed.

The readers' wording differs on how to describe the recovery limitation and where to explain
the retained reference; no wording difference changes either accepted policy. No new retirement
act, evidence form or extra display label is accepted. The separate reported-attempt export
exception and older conformance-wording concern remain outside this decision.

The bead stays open for text, review and publication. This decision makes no capability,
readiness or runtime claim.

comments.text:
## Implementation, one-pass review and closure — failed placements, 2026-11-06

The accepted round-two decision in comment 144000001 is implemented in `SEC-5`, `ARC-43`,
`SEC-6`, the credential format and `CNF-95(l)` and `(m)`, with ADR-0070 and dated pointers
from the earlier decision records. It completes the two original questions on this bead:
the failed attempt's end and the failed first placement's listing, reference and export.

One review pass ran with two independent readers against packet SHA-256
14a73cb912aa38439aebfc5e427add53583bc56699b49d1699268e195b7c6821. Both requested fixes.
Applied once, without another review:

- Qualify every generic rotation end for the particular placement whose reference actually
  ends, including credential rows 12 and 23, listing and wait wording, and the display's
  scan-limit statement. A recorded rotation that ends nothing removes no predecessor key
  and labels no retained predecessor's value unchecked.
- Check the retained named predecessor in fresh output: F1 can write after F2 succeeds,
  and a later dispatched read still redacts F1. Add controls for accidental release and a
  false scan-limit statement; the additional-predecessor case checks that distinction too.
- Make the occupied first-placement sheet position apply to every later unreported

- Check ordinary rotation of F1 after Restore from its sheet, which carries no disposed
  call record, and make retirement at a later eligible recorded act mandatory rather
  than optional. The existing recovery coverage limitation stays explicit at its owner.

One review found the multiple-successor rule insufficiently explicit and the other could
derive it from the accepted rule. The clarification and discriminating case implement the
same policy, not another decision. No new retirement act, evidence form, export field or
importer change is added. The previously accepted completed-before-pre-send core remains.

The separate unvoted reported-attempt export exception, optional failure label and older
conformance-wording concern remain unchosen in their existing records; none is silently
implemented by this closure. No policy branch remains undecided within this bead's original
questions. Specification decision and text work are complete; this is not runtime evidence.

citation, obligation and whitespace checks passed. Full exact-publication-head gates run
alongside publication under the standing fastlane; this record does not claim their result.

title: Decide which machines a reported placement's pre-loss withholding reaches after a Restore
description:
tw-5qs and tw-e42 (ADR-0062) made a recorded operator report final and carried by the sheet. The
`reference_ended` mark (ADR-0060, tw-huu) covers a placement that ended without a report. The two
rules give the machines they reach differently.

**What the text says.**
- For a reported placement P, `SEC-5` says: "After local-store loss nothing restores P's ended
  reference: every job record from before the loss stays withheld for P".
- For the mark, `SEC-5` names its machines: it is set "of Q's machine while that machine stays live
  and of every live machine the exposure ledger records in a bound set with it (`STA-10`)".
- The reported rule names no machine. It does not say whether "withheld for P" reaches a job record
  on a peer in P's bound set, or on a peer of a machine that has since been destroyed.

**The risk.** One reader takes the reported rule to cover only P's own machine, and releases a
peer's pre-loss record that printed P's value. Another takes it to cover every machine. Neither can
point to a sentence.

**Question.** Which machines does a reported placement's pre-loss withholding reach after a Restore:
- the machines the mark would reach (P's machine and every live machine the exposure ledger records
  in a bound set with it);
- or every machine?

Whichever is chosen, add a `CNF-95` branch that checks it, including a peer of a destroyed machine.

Constraints that hold either way:
- "Unscanned bytes MUST be withheld" (`SEC-5`).
- A report never counts as a scan, and is final (ADR-0062).
- The mark's machine scope is not changed (ADR-0060).

Owner question; no normative edit until it is answered.
close_reason: Specified in SEC-5, CNF-95(k) and ADR-0067; closure note in comment 139000001

comments.text:
## Owner pick — a reported placement's pre-loss withholding reaches the mark's machines, 2026-11-06

The question: for a reported placement P, `SEC-5` says "After local-store loss nothing restores
P's ended reference: every job record from before the loss stays withheld for P, and a sheet's
`operator_reported_at` classifies no output." That sentence names no machine, while the
`reference_ended` mark names its machines. After a Restore, does P's pre-loss withholding reach the
mark's machines, every machine, or P's machine only?

**A, the owner's pick after a 2–2 tie.** "After a Restore, every job record from before the loss
stays withheld for a reported P on P's machine and on every live machine the restored exposure
ledger records in a bound set with P's machine (`STA-10`); a machine the ledger never records with
P's machine is released for P (its own references still apply)." Four independent readers answered;
a fifth seat was unavailable. Two recommended A and two recommended B. Whether the text forces an
answer: three said no and one said yes. Which output P's reference scanned before the loss: three
said output on a bound set that included P's machine, and one said every machine's output.

**Shared core the readers gave:**
- The home is `SEC-5`'s operator-report paragraph, which already owns the sentence.
- C is ruled out by `CNF-95(h)`: its scenario has "machines A and M are in one bound set" with
  "output on A is withheld", and "every pre-loss job record stays withheld for P1".
- A destroyed machine's own pre-loss records cannot be collected after a Restore under any option.
- No option touches a theorem: "The formal companion has no placement or scan-reference state".

**Narrowings and widenings:** A narrows the literal, unscoped reach of `SEC-5`'s "every job record
from before the loss stays withheld for P" to P's machine and the live machines the ledger records
in a bound set with it; no earlier owner pick fixed that reach, and ADR-0057 said nothing of
machines. A leaves ADR-0060 unchanged: the mark's setters, machine scope and "nothing clears it"
stand. A leaves ADR-0061 (a rotation never counts as a scan) and ADR-0062 (the report is offered
only while unarmed and is final) unchanged. A changes no assertion of `CNF-95(h)`, whose scenario has
only A and M, recorded together; the text work adds a branch for a machine the ledger never records
with P's machine and for destroyed machines. A weakens no safety rule or `CNF-95` case.

**Detail left to the text work:** the sentence and the `CNF-95` branch. Which ledger the rule reads,
worded as "the sheet's exposure ledger", "the restored exposure ledger" or "the exposure ledger
restored from the sheet", so that a binding made after the Restore does not reach back, goes to the
review pass as a named question.

**Not selected:** B, every machine; C, P's machine only.

This pick is settled and must not be re-asked. It makes no normative edit and no capability,
readiness or runtime claim.

comments.author: owner-decision-lane
comments.text:
## Owner decision — sheetless destructive recovery, 2026-11-02

Selected C: the operator acts at the vendor. Sheetless recovery adds no new destructive authority. For a machine that existing authorization cannot admit, the harness does not gain permission to stop, reinstall or destroy it from a listing, recovery-sheet mapping, newly introduced adoption card or a newly introduced recovery-evidence rule. A listing remains displayed and never relied on for destructive authorization.

The operator handles the old machine at the vendor where an actual route is available. The harness recreates only where its existing credentials, authority, allocation and approval rules permit. Report unavailable remedies honestly; do not promise that every vendor offers a manual destroy or that missing credentials can be recovered. At LNVPS, missing the old seed or allocation index can lose the vendor key, leaving the harness unable to stop, reinstall or confirm deletion. A manual referral alone establishes no deletion, billing cessation or cleared obligation.

Amend the unconditional Cloud destroys and recreates wording in STA-15/STA-22b to express these limits. Correct CNF-84's demand for a LNVPS stop without the vendor key so it agrees with STA-17's refusal and honest incomplete-recovery state. Update affected conformance applicability and checked references after the owner rules change; do not add a competing authorization home.

Existing authority stands unchanged, including SEC-4's abandonment exception for this setup's own create response or admissible key-tied evidence. The decision creates neither general listed-object adoption nor a new sheetless destructive-recovery flow. It does not enable pending bare-seed import, per-machine discovery or T44's coordinated format/recovery amendment. Required retained barriers, identity exclusions, host-pin rules, uncertain outcomes and exposure/billing displays remain in force.

Coordinate stage-1 acquisition with tw-ae7 C: abandonment and a separately started setup do not become an in-setup third rung or an extra order under this recovery decision. The separate dedicated rescue-rekey question remains tw-lq8; no new installation acceptance or reset gate is created under tw-l1l.

Required distinguishing cases: a listed machine without current destructive authority receives no harness destructive dispatch; another account machine is not adopted by selection; a missing LNVPS key yields an explicit unavailable stop/reinstall/deletion-confirmation path; an already authorized abandonment still works under its own proof and approval rules. External/manual action is not reported as confirmed destruction without the existing admitted evidence, and a fresh acquisition uses its own existing approvals.

This owner choice is settled. This record claims neither rule implementation nor completed recovery, and does not claim an unavailable vendor remedy exists.

## Source quotations — current text to preserve or amend

These are quotations of the current source, not claims that the selected amendments have already landed. The selected changes and the queued limits remain as recorded above.

`STA-15` (03-state-and-recovery.md:1012):

> Where a maintained cloud machine's pin is lost with no sheet anyway, the machine is destroyed
> and recreated, which re-runs its first contact and loses its state.

`STA-22b` (03-state-and-recovery.md:842):

> Cloud destroys and recreates (`STA-15`).

`CNF-84` (07-conformance.md:1516):

> Cloud with no
>       sheet exposes destroy/recreate, never an unpinned keyed-rescue login; at LNVPS `ARC-22`'s
>       forms apply instead — a stop with renewal off for the destroy, and for the recreate a
>       reinstall that is a new first contact.

`STA-17` (03-state-and-recovery.md:1135):

> At LNVPS a missing old seed or index
> also loses that machine's vendor key, so the harness can neither reinstall nor stop it; the
> machine remains shown as existing and billed.

`SEC-4` (04-security-model.md:197):

> What an adapter can list of
> the account is displayed and never relied on: a listing is the vendor's word at one moment, and
> the authorization at each dispatch is the enforcement.

`SEC-4` (04-security-model.md:206):

> **The abandonment flow is authorized outside any session.** It MUST act only on machines of
> the unfinished setup whose vendor machine id reached the approved entry through **this setup's
> own** create response, or through evidence tied to the seed-derived key. This authorization is
> checked at dispatch. A mapping imported from a recovery sheet is never enough by itself.
